abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis is a rare but potentially fatal immune-related adverse event (irAE) that may interrupt planned curative treatment for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer. However, the suitability of definitive surgery after recovery from fulminant myocarditis remains unclear.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 53-year-old man with left upper lobe adenocarcinoma and ipsilateral hilar nodal disease was administered four cycles of neoadjuvant cisplatin, pemetrexed, and pembrolizumab, resulting in a partial response. Eighty-six days after the initiation of neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, he developed grade 4 fulminant ICI-associated myocarditis with ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest. Endomyocardial biopsy revealed active lymphocytic myocarditis. The patient required intubation, percutaneous cardiopulmonary support, intra-aortic balloon pumping, continuous hemodiafiltration, high-dose corticosteroids, and prolonged rehabilitation. After his cardiac function recovered, tumor regrowth without distant metastasis was identified. Multidisciplinary reassessment supported surgery because the left ventricular ejection fraction had recovered to 71%, no recurrent malignant arrhythmia had been documented, cardiac biomarkers had improved, prednisolone had been tapered to 10 mg/day, and the disease remained technically resectable. Thoracoscopic-assisted thoracotomy with left upper lobe sleeve resection, pulmonary artery reconstruction, and hilar and mediastinal lymph node dissection was performed 144 days after myocarditis onset, corresponding to 230 days after the initiation of neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. R0 resection was achieved. Surveillance computed tomography showed no evidence of recurrence through 3.5 years after surgery, and the patient was alive at the last follow-up 6.3 years after surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Fulminant ICI-associated myocarditis does not necessarily preclude subsequent curative-intent lung resection. In highly selected patients, surgery may remain feasible after objective cardiac recovery, multidisciplinary reassessment, and shared decision-making with the patient. This case suggests that the acute management of life-threatening cardiovascular irAEs should be undertaken at centers with continuous on-site cardiology support, multidisciplinary care, and access to emergency mechanical circulatory support. Additionally, planning subsequent curative-intent surgery requires multidisciplinary collaboration, ready access to cardiology expertise, and an appropriate pathway for rapid escalation of cardiovascular care.
journal: General thoracic and cardiovascular surgery cases
title: Curative-intent lung resection after recovery from fulminant immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis during neoadjuvant therapy: a case report.

abstract: The contemporary intensive care unit generates an overwhelming magnitude of high-frequency, granular physiological data. However, conventional decision-making for patients requiring temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) remains tethered to reactive, threshold-driven manual adjustments, underutilizing continuous data streams and failing to optimize the complex patient-machine interaction. This review examines the integration of deep neural networks (DNNs) as a candidate strategy for advanced clinical decision support. By identifying a continuous "digital phenotype," hierarchical deep learning architectures signal a shift toward real-time trajectory recognition in tMCS. We establish a four-tier functional taxonomy-prognosticative, descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive-to categorize translational milestones from automated pump-speed optimization to closed-loop homeostatic regulation. Operational challenges are analyzed through the TEIP (Transparency, Explainability, Interpretability, and Performance) Core-Lens Framework, navigating the dynamic equilibrium between computational density and clinical explainability. We further evaluate the evolving global regulatory landscape, advocating for a foundation on verified empirical safety and rigorous clinical trial validation over absolute mathematical transparency in high-density architectures. Implementing a strategic roadmap including context-specific validation, multimodal integration, and human-centered design is quintessential to safely transform passive hardware into intelligent systems. As the field evolves, DNN technology offers a consequential opportunity to advance early cardiopulmonary failure recognition into a clinical reality.
title: Deep Neural Network-Driven Early Recognition in Cardiopulmonary Failure: A Paradigm Shift Underway in Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support?

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) has emerged as a non-pharmacological alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). Following the publication of recent CHAMPION-AF and CLOSURE-AF trials, an updated synthesis of evidence is warranted to clarify the long-term comparative efficacy and safety of LAAO versus OAC in patients with AF.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing LAAO with OAC in adults with AF. A comprehensive search of major databases was performed from inception to April 2026. The primary efficacy outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and stroke. The primary safety outcome was non-procedure-related bleeding. Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Six RCTs including 7,004 patients (3,681 LAAO; 3,323 OAC) were analyzed. No statistically significant difference was observed for MACE (7.5% vs 6.9%; RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.79-1.34) or stroke (3.7% vs 3.2%; RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.80-1.43). LAAO was associated with a significantly lower risk of non-procedure-related bleeding (9.8% vs 16.7%; RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.52-0.77), corresponding to an absolute risk reduction of 6.9% and an approximate number needed to treat of 15 based on crude pooled event rates over the observed trial follow-up. Trial sequential analysis indicated that the accumulated evidence for MACE and stroke remained inconclusive. Comparator-type subgroup analyses showed no significant interaction for MACE (p = 0.67) or stroke (p = 0.81) between contemporary predominantly-DOAC and VKA comparator trials.
CONCLUSIONS: LAAO was associated with lower non-procedure-related bleeding, while no statistically significant differences were observed for MACE or stroke. The available efficacy evidence remains inconclusive regarding equivalence or non-inferiority, and larger trials are needed. These findings support individualized consideration of LAAO when the long-term bleeding burden of anticoagulation is clinically important.
title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion vs Oral Anticoagulation for Stroke Prevention in Atrial Fibrillation: A Meta-Analysis.

abstract:
CONTEXT: Icariin (ICA), a prenylated flavonol glycoside from Epimedii Folium, has been investigated in experimental models relevant to atherosclerosis, myocardial infarction, and ischemic tissue injury.
OBJECTIVES: This review evaluates experimental evidence on ICA in atherosclerotic plaque biology, post-myocardial infarction remodeling, myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury, and cerebral ischemic injury.
METHODS: PubMed and the Web of Science Core Collection were searched from database inception to 19 August 2026, and studies were selected using predefined eligibility criteria. Targeted searches also covered pharmacokinetics, metabolism, toxicology, botanical source, quality control, formulation, and delivery.
RESULTS: In atherosclerosis models, ICA reduced endothelial inflammatory activation, macrophage lipid uptake, vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) proliferation and migration, and lesion burden. Several mechanistic links were tested using pharmacological or genetic perturbation. In vivo studies primarily characterized lesion burden and circulating lipids, with less direct assessment of plaque composition and stability. Post-myocardial infarction and ischemic injury studies reported reductions in fibrosis and ischemic tissue injury, together with reduced mitochondrial injury and changes in inflammatory signaling, apoptosis, and ferroptosis-related processes. Functional improvement was also reported in several models. Few studies measured parent ICA or metabolite concentrations in plaque, myocardium, or brain in the same experiments in which pathological outcomes were assessed.
CONCLUSIONS: Future studies should quantify parent ICA and active metabolites in diseased tissues while assessing plaque composition and stability in the same experiments, so that vascular effects can be related to measured in vivo exposure.
title: Protective effects of icariin in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease: mechanistic basis, post-ischemic protection and translational limitations.
Socioeconomic Status and Cardiovascular Risk-Factor Burden in Patients Presenting With Premature ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates short- to mid-term outcomes following mitral valve repair (MVP) and mitral valve replacement (MVR) among patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR) complicated by substantial left ventricular dilatation (LVD).
METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis enrolling 150 patients diagnosed with DMR and severe LVD who received either MVP or MVR. The median clinical follow-up duration was 55.5 (21.0) months. Propensity score matching (PSM) was conducted to eliminate intergroup baseline disparities. Kaplan-Meier survival curves were generated to estimate short- and mid-term all-cause survival.
RESULTS: Of the 150 enrolled patients with DMR and marked left ventricular dilatation, 56.67% underwent MVR and 43.33% received MVP. The cohort had a median age of 59 (17) years, with female patients making up 23.3% of participants. Preoperative atrial fibrillation occurred in 15.33% of patients, and 92.05% presented with severe baseline mitral valve regurgitation (MR). Analyses before and after PSM showed similar postoperative left ventricular end-diastolic dimension (LVEDD) and New York Heart Association functional class across groups. Significant intergroup differences were detected in postoperative MR (P = 0.017), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (P = 0.005), and global longitudinal strain (GLS) (P = 0.023). Kaplan-Meier curves indicated equivalent postoperative survival for patients who underwent MVP and MVR both before matching (log-rank P = 0.175) and after PSM matching (log-rank P = 0.497).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with DMR and dilated left ventricles (≥6.0 cm), MVR was associated with a greater incidence of postoperative hemorrhage related to long-term oral anticoagulation, whereas MVP conferred a higher risk of recurrent MR. Postoperative mortality was comparable across cohorts; however, preserved left ventricular subclinical systolic function (GLS and LVEF) in the MVP group suggests potential long-term myocardial benefits, which warrants further prospective investigation.
title: Short- and mid-term outcomes of mitral valve repair vs. replacement in degenerative mitral regurgitation with left ventricular enlargement.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, so accurate early risk stratification is essential for predicting adverse events. We investigated whether combining the Creactive protein/albumin ratio (CAR) with the CADILLAC (Controlled Abciximab and Device Investigation to Lower Late Angioplasty Complications) risk score was associated with an increased risk of 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE), and assessed its efficacy in the risk stratification of patients with AMI undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
METHODS AND RESULTS: In total, 554 patients were enrolled. The rate of 1-year MACE was 10.5%. Both the CADILLAC risk category and CAR tertile were independent predictors of 1-year MACE, after adjustment for covariates (hazard ratio [HR] 1.98, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.34-2.92, P=0.001; HR 1.65, 95% CI 1.14-2.37, P=0.007, respectively). Compared to patients with a low CADILLAC risk score and a low CAR tertile, those with a high CADILLAC risk score and a high CAR tertile had the highest 1-year MACE (adjusted HR 8.13, 95% CI 1.88-35.2, P=0.005). Adding CAR to a model that combined the CADILLAC risk score with the baseline factors significantly improved the prediction of 1-year MACE.
CONCLUSIONS: Combining the CAR with the CADILLAC risk score significantly contributed to predicting 1-year MACE in patients with AMI undergoing primary PCI.
title: Combined Prognostic Performance of the CADILLAC Risk Score and C-Reactive Protein/Albumin Ratio in Acute Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) may initially present as acute coronary syndrome and be managed under a presumed ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction pathway before the vessel wall diagnosis is recognized. Management is particularly challenging when extensive intramural hematoma involves left main or bifurcation-related anatomy.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 47-year-old woman presented with recurrent chest pain, cardiac biomarker elevation, and inferior/posterior ST-segment abnormalities. Before SCAD was recognized, recurrent inferior ST-segment elevation was treated under a presumed STEMI pathway, including thrombolysis. Angiography showed a distal left circumflex coronary artery (LCX) double-lumen-like appearance with TIMI grade 3 flow. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) demonstrated a focal distal LCX intimal disruption/fenestration; extensive intramural hematoma involving the imaged distal, mid, and proximal LCX; the LCX ostium; and the imaged left main segment between the bifurcation and the ostium, with marked true-lumen compression. Given hemodynamic stability and the absence of refractory ischemia, conservative management was selected after balancing the anatomical concern against the procedural risks of revascularization. At approximately 3 months, angiography and IVUS showed disappearance of the distal angiographic abnormality and resolution of intramural hematoma within the reassessed segments. During follow-up through approximately 6 years after discharge, the patient reported no recurrent chest pain or unplanned rehospitalization.
CONCLUSION: IVUS clarified lesion morphology and extent not fully defined by angiography, illustrating the complementary roles of angiographic and vessel wall information in case-specific risk assessment. Subsequent resolution does not establish treatment efficacy or support general treatment recommendations. The initiating event and direction of hematoma spread could not be determined from the available imaging.
title: Case Report: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection with intramural hematoma involving the LCX and the left main segment between the bifurcation and the ostium.

abstract: Snakebite envenomation remains a significant neglected tropical disease, particularly in South Asia, where Daboia russelii (Russell's viper) causes substantial morbidity and mortality. Current antivenom therapy is limited by poor efficacy against local tissue damage, high production costs, restricted toxin specificity, and adverse immune reactions, highlighting the need for alternative or adjunct therapeutic strategies. Using an integrated computational and experimental approach, phytocompounds identified from Glycosmis pentaphylla leaf extracts were evaluated as potential inhibitors of major venom proteins. A total of 32 compounds identified by GC-MS were screened against phospholipase A2 (PLA2), snake venom metalloproteinases (SVMPs), snake venom serine proteases (SVSPs), L-amino acid oxidase (LAAO), and snake C-type lectin-like proteins (SNACLECs) using molecular docking. Representative high-affinity protein-ligand complexes were further evaluated by 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations. Pharmacokinetic, toxicity, protein-protein interaction, and pathway enrichment analyses were also performed to assess the therapeutic potential of the identified compounds. Preliminary experimental validation was conducted using trypsin-casein protease inhibition, skim milk agar protease inhibition, and erythrocyte membrane stabilization assays. Compared with N-acetyl cysteine (NAC), β-sitosterol, 3-chloro-5-cholestene, and vitamin E exhibited stronger binding affinities and more stable interactions with multiple venom proteins. Molecular dynamics analyses (RMSD, RMSF, radius of gyration, solvent-accessible surface area, and hydrogen bonding) further supported the stability of the selected protein-ligand complexes. Pharmacokinetic and toxicity predictions indicated acceptable drug-likeness and comparatively safe toxicity profiles for most selected compounds. STRING-based protein-protein interaction and pathway enrichment analyses revealed associations with inflammatory, coagulation, oxidative stress, and extracellular matrix-related pathways involved in venom pathology. The G. pentaphylla extract demonstrated concentration-dependent protease inhibition (56.86% at 5 mg/mL), reduced caseinolytic activity (28.19% inhibition), and significant erythrocyte membrane stabilization (39.23%), providing preliminary experimental support for the computational predictions. Overall, these findings identify G. pentaphylla-derived phytocompounds as potential lead compounds for future antivenom development and provide a computational foundation for subsequent venom-specific biochemical and in vivo validation toward safer and more affordable adjunct therapies for snakebite management.
title: Integrated computational investigation of Glycosmis pentaphylla-derived compounds against major venom proteins of Daboia russelii.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent ischemic events after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) may arise from treated culprit lesions (CLs) or untreated non-CLs (NCLs). However, temporal trends in CL- and NCL-attributed revascularization in contemporary clinical practice remain unclear.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed data from the Mie ACS Registry, a multicenter registry enrolling patients with AMI who underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Patients with previous coronary artery bypass grafting were excluded. The coprimary endpoints were the times to the first CL- and NCL-attributed revascularization over a 2-year follow-up period. Death was treated as a competing event. Temporal trends and predictors were evaluated using competing-risk analyses. Among 6,363 patients, 2,860 were enrolled in 2013-2017 and 3,503 were enrolled in 2018-2022. The cumulative incidence of CL-attributed revascularization was significantly lower in the later era (6.2% vs. 3.5%; P<0.001), whereas NCL-attributed revascularization showed only modest temporal improvement from 2013-2017 to 2018-2022 (6.6% vs. 5.5%, respectively; P=0.091). In multivariable analyses, late-era (2018-2022) enrollment was independently associated with a lower risk of CL-attributed revascularization (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.44-0.71; P<0.001), whereas multivessel disease was the strongest predictor of NCL-attributed revascularization (sHR 2.31; 95% CI 1.84-2.91; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite temporal reductions in CL-attributed revascularization, NCL-attributed events remained relatively unchanged. NCLs continue to represent an important source of residual coronary risk after AMI.
first_author_country: Mie University Graduate School of Medicine Mie Japan
last_author_country: Mie University Graduate School of Medicine Mie Japan
title: Temporal Trends in Culprit- and Non-Culprit Lesion-Attributed Revascularization After Acute Myocardial Infarction: Insights From the Mie ACS Registry.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Heart attacks come in different forms, with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) being two important but distinct types. While doctors can tell them apart in the clinic, it's still unclear exactly how the molecules circulating in the blood differ between the two. Recently, scientists have been looking at circular RNAs (circRNAs), a type of stable non-coding RNA easily found in blood plasma, to see if they can offer new clues beyond traditional heart attack markers. This study set out to find out if the patterns of circRNAs in the blood could reliably tell STEMI and NSTEMI apart, and possibly uncover new, more specific biomarkers for each type.
METHODS: This exploratory observational study included 59 patients with STEMI, 78 with NSTEMI, and 109 hospital-based controls recruited from two hospitals in Eastern Saudi Arabia. Blood samples were collected in EDTA tubes within two hours after the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction. Researchers then used advanced sequencing techniques to look for circRNAs in these blood samples. They compared the circRNA patterns between STEMI, NSTEMI, and control groups, making sure to account for differences in age and other factors. The team also checked how the circRNAs compared with the usual gene activity and tested how well these patterns could tell the two heart attack types apart using a standard accuracy metric.
RESULTS: A total of 297 circRNAs were differentially expressed between STEMI and NSTEMI at a false-discovery rate below 0.05. Several circRNAs, including hsa-PTPN12_000054, hsa-UBAC2_000001, hsa-STK39_000074, hsa-ERP44_000019, and hsa-LINC00299_000001, were enriched in STEMI cases. Meanwhile, circRNAs including hsa-CHD2_000062, hsa-PCCA_000138, hsa-RBM33_000015, and hsa-NPM1_000005 were more abundant in NSTEMI. An exploratory three-circRNA logistic model produced an apparent AUC of 0.866 and a five-fold cross-validated AUC of 0.813. Interestingly, these circRNA changes didn't always match up with changes in the genes they came from, suggesting that circRNAs might be regulated in their own unique way.
CONCLUSION: Plasma circRNA profiles differed between STEMI and NSTEMI in this exploratory discovery cohort. The identified candidates provide a basis for technical confirmation and external validation, but they should not currently be considered clinically validated diagnostic biomarkers.
title: Distinct circular RNA signatures distinguish STEMI from NSTEMI in acute myocardial infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Japanese version of the high bleeding risk (J-HBR) criteria identifies patients with HBR undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). We evaluated whether routine J-HBR calculation and peri-procedural discussion on dual-antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) duration were associated with changes in DAPT practice and clinical outcomes.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively evaluated 793 patients who underwent PCI between August 2019 and August 2021. Routine J-HBR calculation and peri-procedural discussion on DAPT duration were introduced in August 2020, and patients were categorized into post- and pre-J-HBR groups. The median DAPT duration was 174 and 188 days (P=0.47), and guideline-directed DAPT duration was achieved in 62.6% and 56.9%, respectively (P=0.13) in the post- and pre-J-HBR groups. Clinical outcomes did not differ significantly between groups, including net adverse clinical events (hazard ratio [HR], 1.08; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.77-1.52; P=0.65), major cardiovascular or cerebrovascular events (HR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.44-1.32; P=0.34), and major bleeding (HR, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.90-1.89; P=0.17). Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis showed that routine J-HBR calculation and peri-procedural discussion were not associated with a significant reduction in major bleeding (HR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.65-1.46; P=0.88).
CONCLUSIONS: Routine J-HBR calculation and peri-procedural discussion on DAPT duration were not associated with significant changes in overall DAPT duration or clinical outcomes.
first_author_country: Japanese Red Cross Aichi Medical Center Nagoya Daini Hospital Nagoya Japan
last_author_country: Nagoya University Graduate School of Medicine Nagoya Japan
title: Limited Impact of High Bleeding Risk Calculation and Peri-Procedural Discussion on Dual-Antiplatelet Therapy Duration and Clinical Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nutritional status at discharge is a prognostic factor in acute heart failure (AHF) patients, but its relationship with early-phase nutritional therapy in the cardiovascular intensive care unit (CICU) remains unclear, so we evaluated the effects of HF severity, respiratory management, and nutritional dosage on nutritional status in AHF patients.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analyzed 141 of 160 AHF patients admitted to the CICU in 2021, excluding those with acute coronary syndrome, who had died, or had been discharged early. Patients were divided into 3 groups by respiratory support: invasive ventilation (IPPV, n=21), non-invasive ventilation (NPPV, n=36), and other forms of oxygen supplementation (O2S, n=84). The mean age of the patients was 72±15 years. On day 3, the IPPV group received less nutrition than the O2S group, but by day 7 there was no significant difference among the groups in the nutritional doses administered. No significant differences in the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) at discharge were observed among the groups. Multiple regression analysis identified the energy (standardized β=0.210, P=0.029) and protein (standardized β=0.248, P=0.007) doses on day 3 as being correlated with the GNRI at discharge, independent of HF severity or respiratory management.
CONCLUSIONS: The nutritional dose on day 3, rather than HF severity, respiratory management or the day 7 nutritional dose, may be associated with the GNRI at discharge.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) may be overlooked in patients undergoing hemodialysis (HD) because anemia is commonly attributed to renal anemia and treated with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. MDS is also associated with an increased risk of bacterial infections due to neutropenia and qualitative immune dysfunction. We report recurrent invasive methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) infections in a patient undergoing HD with concomitant MDS.
CASE PRESENTATION: The patient was a 76-year-old man undergoing HD for end-stage kidney disease due to nephrosclerosis who was referred to our hospital because of persistent anemia despite high-dose darbepoetin alfa therapy. He had a history of CHOP therapy for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and his MDS was considered possibly therapy related. Bone marrow aspiration revealed trilineage dysplasia and 3.4% blasts without chromosomal abnormalities, leading to a diagnosis of MDS with multilineage dysplasia. Approximately 1 year later, he developed persistent fever. Blood cultures yielded MSSA, and imaging studies revealed septic pulmonary embolism and multiple cerebral infarctions. He improved after intravenous cefepime therapy. Twenty-two months later, he developed fever and left shoulder pain. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed an abscess in the left subscapularis muscle, and MSSA was isolated from the drainage fluid after CT-guided drainage. He improved with drainage and antibiotic therapy. In both episodes, the neutrophil count was preserved.
CONCLUSION: This case illustrates recurrent invasive MSSA infections in a non-neutropenic HD patient with possibly therapy-related MDS. HD-related factors should be carefully evaluated as common causes of recurrent S. aureus infection, and MDS may represent an additional, unproven host factor. MDS should be considered in ESA-resistant anemia in HD patients, particularly in those with a history of cytotoxic chemotherapy.

title: Recurrent Invasive Staphylococcus aureus Infections in a Non-Neutropenic Hemodialysis Patient With Myelodysplastic Syndrome: A Case Report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contrast-associated nephropathy is a complication of cardiovascular procedures. Although contrast volume is a risk factor for acute kidney injury, its impact on medium- to long-term renal function remains unknown. This study aimed to investigate this association in patients undergoing repeated percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI).
METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included patients undergoing repeated PCIs between 2003 and 2023, with intervals of ≥7 and ≤ 365 days between procedures. Renal function was classified by "Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes" (KDIGO) staging system. The maximum allowable contrast dose (MACD) was retrospectively calculated as individual threshold. Primary endpoint was progression to a higher KDIGO stage at readmission. Secondary endpoints included changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR).
RESULTS: In total 6714 patients were included (mean age 67.2 years; 80.2% male; KDIGO stage analysis available for 6611; median interval between procedures 127 days). Baseline mean eGFR was 74.4 mL/min/1.73 m2. Median contrast volume was 220 mL, and median MACD 300 mL. At readmission, mean eGFR was 72.2 mL/min/1.73 m2, 1700 Patients (25.7%) showed KDIGO stage progression. Neither contrast volume nor MACD exceedance was associated with renal deterioration. However, predispositions (diabetes mellitus, arterial hypertension, age), clinical presentation (STEMI, NSTEMI) and the vascular access route were significantly associated with adverse renal outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Contrast volume and MACD exceedance during PCI was not associated with deterioration of medium- to long-term renal function.

journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
title: Impact of contrast volume on medium- to long-term renal function in patients undergoing repeated percutaneous coronary interventions.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Aortic valve replacement (AVR) is the definitive treatment for severe aortic valve disease, yet outcome data from Africa remain scarce. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed survival, mortality, and major adverse events after AVR across Africa.
METHODS: Adhering to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for studies reporting AVR outcomes in African populations, covering randomized trials, cohort studies, case series, and case reports. Subgroup analyses were conducted by AVR modality: surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), minimally invasive surgery (MICS), and transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Study quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool 2 and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Outcomes included survival, mortality, echocardiographic improvements, and valve- or procedure-related complications.
RESULTS: Of 2547 studies screened, 21 studies involving 1303 patients across 6 African countries were included; 15 (71.4%) studies were from Egypt. Mean age was 60.4 years; 43.3% were female. Aortic stenosis (70.4%) and regurgitation (64.0%) predominated. Modalities included SAVR (45.1%), minimally invasive surgery (27.8%), and transcatheter aortic valve implantation (27.1%). Technical success rate was high (97.5%-100%). Complications included arrhythmias (16.0%), postoperative bleeding (15.0%), paravalvular leak (5.0%), pacemaker requirement (6.0%), stroke (5.0%), and myocardial infarction (3.0%). Reoperation rate was 4.4%. Thirty-day mortality was 5.0% (95% CI. 3.1%-8.1%), with 1-year and 5-year survival of 93.2% and 91.0%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: AVR outcomes in Africa show favorable success and survival rate although below optimal benchmarks despite resource constraints. However, results are not generalizable continent-wide, given the heavy geographic skew. Complications including arrhythmias and postoperative bleeding necessitate enhanced perioperative protocols.
title: Outcomes, survival, mortality, and major adverse events in aortic valve replacement surgeries in Africa: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract:
AIM: We aimed to conduct an exploratory investigation on the association between bowel diameter on early-phase abdominal computed tomography (CT) and neurological outcomes in patients undergoing extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA).
METHODS: This observational study included patients who underwent ECPR for OHCA and abdominal CT before intensive care unit admission between January 2015 and December 2021 at a tertiary emergency medical center. Maximum bowel diameter was measured with a picture archiving and communication system by an investigator blinded to outcomes. The primary endpoint was unfavorable neurological outcomes at 1 month, defined as Cerebral Performance Category 3-5. The discriminatory ability of bowel diameter was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).
RESULTS: Data from 181 patients were analyzed (median age, 57 years; 84.5% male). Bowel diameter demonstrated a weak ability to predict unfavorable neurological outcomes, with an AUC of 0.58 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47-0.70). However, higher discriminatory performance was observed in subgroups of patients aged ≥ 65 years (AUC, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.69-0.96) and those with initial nonshockable rhythms (AUC, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.47-0.91).
CONCLUSION: The results of this exploratory investigation suggest that bowel diameter may represent a potential adjunctive marker associated with functional outcomes post-ECPR for OHCA.
title: Early-Phase Computed Tomography Bowel Diameter and Neurological Outcomes Post-Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hepatic artery complications after liver transplantation are uncommon but potentially catastrophic because the biliary tree depends entirely on the arterial blood supply. Graft hepatic artery dissection (GHAD) is extremely rare following living donor liver transplantation (LDLT), and optimal management strategies remain unclear.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 68-year-old man with hepatocellular carcinoma and underlying alcohol-related cirrhosis underwent right-lobe LDLT. During donor hepatectomy, intimal dissection of the graft hepatic artery, extending deep into the liver parenchyma, was identified. After arterial reconstruction, intraoperative Doppler ultrasound demonstrated absent arterial flow. The abdomen was closed, and the patient was transferred for urgent endovascular intervention. Angiography confirmed compromised arterial inflow, and a drug-eluting stent was deployed across the arterial anastomosis, followed by catheter-directed thrombolysis using alteplase. Postoperatively, the patient developed intra-abdominal bleeding requiring emergency re-laparotomy for hemostasis. Despite this complication, hepatic arterial perfusion was successfully restored. Liver function gradually improved, and follow-up imaging confirmed adequate graft perfusion. The patient was discharged 3 weeks after transplantation with preserved graft function.
DISCUSSION: GHAD is a rare but serious vascular complication that may result in graft ischemia, biliary complications, and graft failure if not promptly treated. When surgical revision is not feasible, endovascular techniques - including stent placement and thrombolysis - can serve as effective salvage strategies. However, thrombolytic therapy carries a significant risk of hemorrhagic complications, requiring careful postoperative monitoring.
CONCLUSION: Early diagnosis and multidisciplinary management are essential for the successful salvage of GHAD after LDLT.
journal: International journal of surgery case reports
title: Endovascular salvage of graft hepatic artery dissection with intrahepatic extension following right lobe living donor liver transplantation: a case report with literature review.

abstract: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is a prevalent condition historically associated with high mortality and underrecognition. While medical therapy remains common, standalone surgical interventions involve significant perioperative risks. This has led to the emergence of transcatheter tricuspid valve interventions (TTVI) as a vital alternative for high-risk patients. Initiated and led by the Gulf Interventional Society, a multidisciplinary panel of experts was brought together to develop the current evidence and formulate a regional consensus and evidence-based recommendations for the management of tricuspid valve regurgitation in the Gulf region. TR is classified into primary (10%) and secondary (90%) types, with secondary TR further divided into atrial and ventricular subtypes. Evaluation relies on multimodality imaging, with echocardiography as the cornerstone and cardiac magnetic resonance for right ventricular assessment. While medical therapy focuses on decongestion, it does not modify TR progression. Surgical repair remains the gold standard for low-to-intermediate risk patients, but early referral is critical to avoid futile procedures in advanced disease. TTVI options, including edge-to-edge repair and replacement, are expanding in the Gulf, though regional adoption is hampered by fragmented healthcare systems and late presentations. Effective TR management in the Gulf requires a transition toward patient-centered care, early identification by primary care physicians, and a multidisciplinary "Heart Team" approach. Integrating digital health tools and establishing regional registries are essential to improving clinical outcomes and survival.
journal: Heart views : the official journal of the Gulf Heart Association
title: Management of Tricuspid Valve Regurgitation Consensus Recommendations.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) increases cardiovascular disease risk through systemic inflammation, particularly through elevated C-reactive protein (CRP). This study investigated whether CRP stratification predicts mortality and cardiovascular events in OSA patients.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis using the TriNetX Research Network, encompassing electronic health records from 130 healthcare institutions. Adults (ages 18-90 years) with OSA were stratified by CRP concentration: elevated (≥ 3.0 mg/L) versus low (≤ 2.9 mg/L). After propensity score matching for demographics and comorbidities, 240,727 participants per cohort were followed for five years. Primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes included cardiovascular events, arrhythmias, and acute kidney injury.
RESULTS: Elevated CRP was associated with significantly higher all-cause mortality (11.3% versus 7.0%; HR 1.695, 95% CI 1.662-1.727; p < 0.001). The elevated CRP group demonstrated heightened cardiovascular risk: cardiogenic shock (1.0% versus 0.5%; HR 2.003), heart failure (9.8% versus 6.5%; HR 1.594), pulmonary hypertension (4.9% versus 3.4%; HR 1.508), and acute kidney injury (11.0% versus 6.4%; HR 1.825), all p < 0.001. Arrhythmic complications were also increased: atrial fibrillation/flutter (6.3% versus 4.8%; HR 1.372) and ventricular tachycardia (2.3% versus 1.8%; HR 1.388), both p < 0.001.
CONCLUSION: Elevated CRP constitutes a robust predictor of mortality and cardiovascular morbidity in OSA populations. Assessment of inflammatory biomarkers may enhance risk stratification, informing intensified monitoring and targeted therapeutic interventions.
title: C-Reactive Protein as a Predictor of Cardiovascular Events and Mortality in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Propensity-Matched Analysis Using the TriNetX Research Network.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement is now a leading treatment for severe symptomatic aortic stenosis across the risk spectrum. The choice between transcatheter and surgical aortic valve replacement remains a shared decision, particularly for patients aged 65 to 80 years. Despite extensive device-level randomized evidence and procedural standardization, periprocedural care pathways remain variable across programs. This turnkey order set integrates contemporary guidelines and consensus documents into a practical order set for the periprocedural care of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
METHODS: Subject matter experts translated existing peer-reviewed society guidelines, expert consensus documents, and randomized trial evidence, identified through a structured PICO-framed (population, intervention, comparator, outcome) literature review, into a sample turnkey order set. Orders derived from consistent Class I or IIa (or equivalent) recommendations across referenced documents appear in the order set in bold type. Orders that were inconsistently Class I or IIa, Class IIb, or supported by peer-reviewed evidence appear in italic type.
RESULTS: Preprocedural care centers on interdisciplinary Heart Team evaluation, frailty and cognition assessment, baseline conduction risk stratification, anemia and iron deficiency screening, structured antithrombotic and endocrine medication management, and weight-based antibiotic prophylaxis. Intraprocedural care prioritizes ultrasound-guided femoral access, procedural sedation when feasible, normothermia, contrast minimization, and balanced procedural anticoagulation. Postprocedural care emphasizes telemetry-guided conduction monitoring, single antiplatelet therapy in patients without an indication for oral anticoagulation, oral anticoagulation alone in those with an existing indication, and early mobilization. Standardized discharge criteria target next-day discharge in appropriately selected transfemoral patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Comprehensive periprocedural pathways for transcatheter aortic valve replacement have been demonstrated to shorten length of stay without compromising safety. This turnkey order set translates contemporary guideline recommendations into actionable orders to facilitate standardized adoption of best practices across programs. The composite pathway has not been prospectively validated.
title: Enhanced recovery after surgery turnkey order set for periprocedural care of the patient undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major modifiable risk factor for coronary artery disease, and cardiovascular events can represent the first clinical manifestation of undiagnosed DM. Our study aims to determine the incidence of newly detected cardiovascular risk factors, including DM, prediabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and smoking, among patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in Qatar.
METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study was included all patients admitted with ST-or non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (MI) to Heart Hospital, Qatar, between March 1, 2015, and December 31, 2020. Data were extracted from electronic records, including newly diagnosed DM was defined as hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) ≥6.5%; prediabetes as HbA1c 5.6%-6.4%; dyslipidemia as low-density lipoprotein (LDL) ≥3.3 mmol/L; and familial hyperlipidemia as LDL ≥4.9 mmol/L with a family history. Smoking and hypertension were also recorded.
RESULTS: Among 10,450 patients, the mean age of ACS was 51 ± 11 years, and 92.4% were male, 13.2% had newly diagnosed DM, and 21.2% met prediabetes criteria. Dyslipidemia, hypertension, and smoking were newly identified in 30.3%, 38.9%, and 27.3%, respectively. These findings suggest that ACS onset occurred at a markedly younger age compared to international cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: Undiagnosed cardiovascular risk factors, particularly DM and prediabetes, are highly prevalent and may be associated with earlier MI. Thus, early screening and preventive strategies should be more targeted and tailored to reflect the distinct cardiometabolic risk profiles of Middle Eastern populations.
journal: Heart views : the official journal of the Gulf Heart Association
title: Diabetes Screening Age and the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force Guideline: Does One Size Fit All? Insights from the Middle East.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND IMPORTANCE: Focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) is a benign liver lesion usually associated with vascular abnormalities. Neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), on the other hand, frequently metastasize to the liver and typically appear as hypervascular lesions. The coexistence of FNH and diffuse hepatic metastases from an ileal NET is exceptionally rare and represents a major diagnostic challenge because both entities may present as hypervascular liver lesions, potentially leading to misdiagnosis and inappropriate management.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 56-year-old woman with a history of epilepsy treated with sodium valproate presented with progressive right upper quadrant pain and abdominal distension. Imaging showed a large hepatic lesion suggestive of FNH along with multiple hypervascular liver nodules suspicious for metastases. A CT-guided liver biopsy demonstrated metastatic well-differentiated NET with a Ki-67 index below 2%. Laboratory tests revealed elevated chromogranin A and urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid levels. The patient also had chronic diarrhea and moderate tricuspid regurgitation consistent with carcinoid syndrome. A ^68 Ga-DOTANOC positron emission tomography/computed tomography localized the primary tumor to the ileum. The integration of radiological, functional, and histopathological findings enabled accurate diagnosis and appropriate therapeutic planning. Surgical resection of the primary tumor was performed, followed by long-acting octreotide therapy. The patient remained clinically stable, with no progression of the hepatic lesions during follow-up.
CLINICAL DISCUSSION: The presence of multiple hypervascular liver lesions in patients with NETs raises important diagnostic issues, especially when benign and malignant lesions coexist. This case demonstrates the value of integrating hepatobiliary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), histopathological confirmation, and functional imaging to accurately distinguish FNH from metastatic disease and to guide appropriate therapeutic management.
CONCLUSION: The coexistence of FNH and diffuse liver metastases from an ileal NET is rare. This case highlights the pivotal role of a multimodal diagnostic approach combining hepatobiliary MRI, functional imaging, and targeted histopathological confirmation to distinguish benign from malignant hypervascular liver lesions, avoid diagnostic pitfalls, and optimize patient management.
journal: International journal of surgery case reports
title: Coexisting focal nodular hyperplasia and diffuse hepatic metastases from an ileal neuroendocrine tumor: a case report and literature review.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The factors associated with mortality following acute coronary syndrome (ACS) based on patient satisfaction are unknown. The objective was to describe and compare factors associated with 1-year mortality following ACS according to high versus low patient satisfaction with hospital stay, doctors, and nurses.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In a registry of 3565 patients presenting with ACS to 29 hospitals across 4 countries, we grouped patients by self-reported satisfaction with hospital stay reported at 1-month following ACS. The primary outcome was all-cause 1-year mortality following ACS, excluding patients with mortality before the initial 30-day follow-up. We examined associations of patient and hospitalization factors with risk of 1-year all-cause mortality in logistic regression models, unadjusted and adjusted for Global Registry of Acute Coronary Event (GRACE) risk score, reported as odds ratio (OR; 95% confidence interval).
RESULTS: In models adjusting for GRACE risk score, in the low satisfaction category, women, compared with men, had statistically similar odds of mortality (adjusted OR: 1.43 [0.99-2.04]). Lack of formal education (vs. any education) was associated with higher odds of mortality in the low satisfaction (aOR: 1.99 [1.33-3.04]; P < 0.01) and high satisfaction (aOR: 3.06 [1.93-5.00]; P < 0.001) categories (P interaction = 0.30). Lack of employment (vs. employment) was associated with similar higher odds of mortality in the low satisfaction (aOR: 6.37 [2.83-18.25]; P < 0.001) and high satisfaction (aOR: 2.58 [1.40-5.21]; P < 0.01) categories (P interaction = 0.08). Generally comparable results were obtained when analyzed by patient satisfaction with doctors and with nurses.
CONCLUSIONS: Education and employment were major factors associated with higher 1-year mortality following ACS, independent of patient satisfaction, and may inform tailored educational and outreach interventions to reduce mortality.
journal: Heart views : the official journal of the Gulf Heart Association
title: Factors Associated with Mortality following Acute Coronary Syndrome According to Patient Satisfaction.

abstract: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains a leading global cause of morbidity and mortality. Healthcare systems worldwide have established national guidelines to facilitate the timely identification and transfer of patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) to centers capable of performing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Typically, ST-segment elevation (STE) on an electrocardiogram (ECG) is indicative of STEMI, prompting early intervention. However, rare cases of STE have been documented in the setting of sepsis or septic shock, with subsequent coronary angiography or imaging revealing normal coronary arteries. There is limited information regarding the exact mechanisms responsible for STE in the context of sepsis. We report the case of a 79-year-old Indian female who presented with epigastric pain and vomiting. Her initial ECG showed STE in leads I, aVL, and V2, accompanied by markedly elevated cardiac biomarkers. In accordance with the national STEMI network protocol, she received prehospital dual antiplatelet therapy and intravenous heparin before hospital arrival and was transferred directly for primary PCI. She was initially managed as a case of ACS; however, coronary angiography demonstrated normal coronary arteries. Further evaluation led to the diagnosis of septic shock secondary to extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli urosepsis, requiring mechanical ventilation, four concurrent vasopressors, and continuous venovenous hemodiafiltration, with complete clinical recovery. Notably, her ECG abnormalities resolved within 72 h following prompt management of the septic shock. While STEMI remains the most common cause of STE on ECG, sepsis and septic shock are rare but important differential diagnoses. The underlying pathophysiology may involve inflammatory myocardial injury, transient coronary vasospasm, or global hypoperfusion. This case highlights the critical importance of recognizing septic shock as a potentially life-threatening STEMI mimic, to avoid unnecessary invasive interventions and to guide appropriate, targeted management.
journal: Heart views : the official journal of the Gulf Heart Association
title: A Diagnostic Dilemma: Urosepsis Mimicking ST-elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence linking pre- and post-transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) blood pressure (BP) with cardiovascular outcomes is scarce. This study investigated the associations of pre- and post-TAVI BP and their changes as a continuous variable with cardiovascular outcomes.
METHODS: Patients undergoing TAVI at a tertiary university hospital between 2011 and 2025 with office BP available before and after TAVI were included. The primary outcome was a composite of major adverse cardiac events (MACE) at 1 year. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models incorporating restricted cubic splines for continuous variables were fitted.
RESULTS: Among 1191 patients, BP remained relatively stable from pre-TAVI to 1-year follow-up. Both discharge systolic BP and absolute changes therein from pre- to post-TAVI were significantly associated with MACE at 1 year (P<0.001 for both), whereas baseline systolic BP showed no significant association. BP values <115 mm Hg or >143 mm Hg were associated with a higher risk of MACE 1 year after TAVI. A decrease in systolic BP of -5 to -25 mm Hg was also associated with a lower risk of MACE compared with no change.
CONCLUSIONS: While BP remains generally stable in the year following TAVI, both very low and high systolic BP at discharge were associated with higher 1-year MACE. Furthermore, moderate decreases in systolic BP from baseline to discharge appear to be protective. These findings highlight the potential prognostic value of BP optimization during TAVI follow-up and support the role of BP measurements as a clinically translatable, independently associated with long-term outcomes after TAVI.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
title: Impact of Continuous Baseline and Discharge Blood Pressure on Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study sought to determine the impact of left ventricular size on clinical outcomes after a microaxial flow pump was surgically implanted.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we included patients who received a surgical microaxial left ventricular assist device from May 2020 to February 2024 at 2 high-volume centers in the United States. Patients were categorized into 2 groups based on their preimplant left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD): "small LVEDD," defined as LVEDD ≤5.5 cm, and "large LVEDD," defined as LVEDD >5.5 cm, respectively. End points were all-cause death at 30 days after device implantation, in-hospital death, death 30-days after discharge, and survival at 30-month follow-up.
RESULTS: Two-hundred sixty-two patients received an Impella 5.5. Preimplant LVEDD was documented in 194 (74%) patients, where 50 patients had LVEDD ≤5.5 cm and 144 patients had LVEDD >5.5 cm. Patients with a small LVEDD had a higher rate of all-cause death at 30 days after device implantation (32% versus 11.8%, P=0.002), in-hospital death (42% versus 20.1%, P=0.004), and death 30 days after discharge (44% versus 20.8%, P=0.003). In adjusted analyses, patients with a greater LVEDD had 62% decreased risk of long-term death (hazard ratio, 0.39 [95% CI, 0.19-0.76]; P=0.001), compared with patients with a smaller LVEDD.
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world, all-comer study, we found that patients with reduced left ventricular dimension who required an Impella 5.5 had worse outcomes. Further research is warranted to recapitulate our observations across more centers.
first_author_country: New York Presbyterian Hospital New York NY USA
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
last_author_country: New York Presbyterian Hospital New York NY USA
title: Left Ventricular End-Diastolic Diameter Predicts Clinical Outcomes in Patients Supported With Surgically Implanted Microaxial Flow Pump.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite high recanalization rates with endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion stroke, a large proportion of patients remain disabled. This study aims to investigate the clinical impact of persistent hypoperfusion that was detected immediately after recanalization.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with large vessel occlusion with near-complete or complete recanalization, perfusion maps were generated from post-recanalization digital subtraction angiography. Focal hypoperfusion within the ischemic territory was detected and categorized as regional or cortical according to spatial distribution. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0 to 2). The associations of no-reflow and outcomes were examined by multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 375 patients (median age 69 [interquartile range 57-77] years; 67.5% men), persistent hypoperfusion was detected in 29.6% of patients. Patients with hypoperfusion had higher baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (median 14 versus 12, P=0.076) and more thrombectomy passes (P=0.021). The presence of persistent hypoperfusion was strongly associated with reduced functional independence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=0.23, 95% CI 0.13-0.39, P<0.001), higher rates of hemorrhagic transformation (aOR=1.88, 95% CI 1.14-3.11; P=0.013) and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (aOR=2.95, 95% CI 1.20-7.23; P=0.018). Quantitative analysis revealed minimum regional cerebral blood flow as a key factor of functional outcome (aOR=1.67, 95% CI 1.07-2.60; P=0.023). There is no significant agreement with 24-hour computed tomography perfusion-defined hypoperfusion (κ=0.106, P=0.524).
CONCLUSIONS: Persistent hypoperfusion could be detected immediately post-recanalization in one-third of successfully treated large vessel occlusion strokes. The adverse impact to functional outcome highlights its potential as an intraprocedural biomarker for future adjunctive therapies.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
title: Persistent Hypoperfusion on Post-Recanalization Digital Subtraction Angiography Perfusion Maps in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diagnosing myocardial infarction in patients with prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains challenging, primarily because of lower diagnostic accuracy of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn). cMyC (cardiac myosin-binding protein C), because of its faster release kinetics and greater abundance, may offer improved diagnostic performance in this population.
METHODS: The diagnostic accuracy of cMyC was directly compared with that of hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI in a prospective, international, multicenter, diagnostic study enrolling adult patients presenting to the emergency department with acute chest discomfort. Final diagnoses were centrally adjudicated by 2 independent cardiologists using all available clinical and study-specific data, including imaging and serial hs-cTnT measurements. Patients were stratified according to the presence or absence of prior CABG.
RESULTS: Among 4752 patients, 387 (8%) had prior CABG (median age, 75 years; 86% men). The incidence of myocardial infarction was significantly higher in patients with prior CABG (38% versus 16%; P<0.001). In the CABG group, the diagnostic accuracy of cMyC as quantified by the area under the curve was 0.88 (95% CI, 0.85-0.92), which was comparable but not superior to that of hs-cTnT (0.89 [95% CI, 0.86-0.92]) and hs-cTnI (0.88 [95% CI, 0.84-0.91]). These findings were consistent across alternative high-sensitivity cMyC assays.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with prior CABG, cMyC demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy for myocardial infarction, but not superior to established hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI assays.
REGISTRATION: URL: clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT00470587.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
title: Cardiac Myosin-Binding Protein C for Diagnosis of Myocardial Infarction in Patients With Prior Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.

abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the effects of early evolocumab plus atorvastatin on lipid metabolism, circulating endothelial biomarkers, and inflammation in STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI).MethodsIn this single-center, open-label trial, 90 patients were randomized 1:1 to atorvastatin 20 mg/day (control, n=45) or atorvastatin 20 mg/day plus evolocumab 140 mg biweekly (combination, n=45) for 12 weeks. One patient withdrew from the combination group at day 28; last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) was applied to impute missing 12-week endpoints for the withdrawn participant. All 90 randomized patients were included in the intention-to-treat (ITT) analytic population. Lipid profiles, endothelial biomarkers, inflammatory cytokines, and safety outcomes were assessed at baseline and 12 weeks. Standard Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) with 12-week value as dependent variable and corresponding baseline level as covariate was used to compare between-group treatment effects for normally distributed outcomes; non-parametric tests were applied for non-normally distributed data. All secondary biomarker, cardiac function and safety analyses were predefined as exploratory without multiplicity adjustment.ResultsBaseline characteristics were well-balanced. The primary endpoint-change in LDL-C from baseline-was significantly greater in the combination group (adjusted mean difference: -0.31 mmol/L, 95% CI: -0.60 to -0.02, P=0.037). A significantly higher proportion achieved the guideline-recommended LDL-C target of <1.4 mmol/L (48.89% vs. 22.2%, P=0.007). Secondary endpoints showed favorable changes in nitric oxide, endothelin-1, and sICAM-1 (all P<0.05), and a significant reduction in IL-6 by non-parametric testing (P=0.005). No significant between-group differences were observed for other biomarkers, cardiac function indices, or adverse events (all P>0.05).ConclusionsIn this small, single-center trial, early evolocumab added to moderate-intensity atorvastatin was associated with additional LDL-C reduction and favorable changes in selected circulating endothelial biomarkers and IL-6 over 12 weeks in STEMI patients post-PPCI, no major safety signal was observed in this short-term study. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials using guideline-directed high-intensity statin therapy as the standard of care. Chinese Clinical Trial Register submission ID: PID343553 (application currently under administrative review, not publicly released).
title: Effects of evolocumab on lipid profile and circulating endothelial biomarkers in patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention.

abstract: BackgroundPerioperative myocardial injury (PMI) and perioperative myocardial infarction (PMIn) are common, often clinically silent complications after noncardiac surgery and are associated with substantial short- and long-term mortality. Surgical stress promotes a prothrombotic milieu through platelet activation, coagulation cascade amplification, impaired fibrinolysis, endothelial dysfunction, and plaque destabilization.PurposeThis narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the thrombotic mechanisms, diagnostic challenges, and antithrombotic management of PMI/PMIn, with emphasis on risk stratification using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and thrombogenicity biomarkers.MethodsMajor perioperative cohort studies, randomized trials, scientific statements, and international guidelines were reviewed, including VISION, MANAGE, POISE, PANDA, the 2021 American Heart Association scientific statement, the 2024 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) perioperative guideline, and the 2022 European Society of Cardiology guideline.ResultsMost perioperative ischemic injury is clinically silent and frequently reflects oxygen supply-demand mismatch, whereas atherothrombotic plaque rupture with coronary thrombosis represents an important minority. Serial high-sensitivity troponin surveillance is central to detection, but interpretation requires exclusion of nonischemic causes and integration with electrocardiography, echocardiography, clinical context, and coronary anatomy. CCTA identifies vulnerable coronary anatomy, whereas D-dimer and thromboelastography-derived platelet-fibrin clot strength characterize a complementary vulnerable-blood phenotype. Antithrombotic therapy should be individualized: antiplatelet therapy and invasive evaluation are appropriate for Type 1 PMIn when bleeding risk permits, whereas dabigatran reduced major vascular complications in selected patients with myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery (MINS) in MANAGE.ConclusionsA multimodal strategy integrating clinical risk, coronary anatomy, postoperative troponin surveillance, and thrombogenicity assessment may improve perioperative risk discrimination and guide individualized prevention and treatment.
journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
title: Perioperative Myocardial Injury and Infarction: Thrombotic Mechanisms, Diagnostic Challenges, and Antithrombotic Management.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) remains an important complication following primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). In emergency settings, preventive strategies must be rapid and compatible with timely reperfusion. This study evaluated whether a single preprocedural bolus of high-concentration sodium bicarbonate was associated with a lower incidence of CIN.
METHODS: In this prospective randomised study, 110 STEMI patients undergoing PPCI at two tertiary centres were enrolled. All patients received standard care, including isotonic saline hydration. Participants were assigned to saline hydration alone or saline plus a single intravenous bolus of 20 mEq of 8.4% sodium bicarbonate administered 5-10 min before contrast exposure. The primary endpoint was CIN within 48 ± 12 h, defined as an increase in serum creatinine ≥0.5 mg/dL or ≥25% from baseline.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were generally comparable, although baseline blood urea nitrogen was higher and estimated glomerular filtration rate lower in the control group. CIN occurred more frequently in controls than in the sodium bicarbonate group (16.4% vs. 1.8%; p = 0.008). Renal function trajectories also favoured sodium bicarbonate. However, sodium bicarbonate did not remain an independent predictor of CIN after multivariable adjustment (OR 0.061, 95% CI 0.003-1.205; p = 0.066).
CONCLUSIONS: Sodium bicarbonate administration was associated with a lower unadjusted incidence of CIN. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger multicentre studies.
title: Effect of a single high-concentration sodium bicarbonate bolus on contrast-induced nephropathy in STEMI patients undergoing Primary PCI: a prospective randomized study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) reflect accumulated microvascular brain injury in small vessel disease, yet their impact on acute-phase circulating biomarker profile after ischemic stroke remains poorly defined. We examined whether WMH burden is associated with greater circulating biomarker levels in acute ischemic stroke, independent of infarct size.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a cohort from a prospective single-center registry of patients with MRI-confirmed ischemic stroke without large-vessel occlusion who were treated with intravenous thrombolysis. WMH and infarct volumes were quantitatively measured on MRI. Circulating neurofilament light chain (NfL) and selected inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers were obtained at the time of thrombolysis. Associations between WMH burden and biomarker levels were assessed using multivariable linear regression.
RESULTS: Among 168 patients (median age 69 years; 39% women), greater WMH volume was independently associated with higher circulating NfL levels (fold-change 1.25, 95% CI 1.12-1.41; p < 0.001), even after adjustment for infarct volume. The standardized effect of WMH volume on NfL was comparable to that of infarct volume. In contrast, associations between WMH burden and inflammatory or endothelial biomarkers were weak and inconsistent after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: WMH burden is independently associated with higher NfL in the acute phase of ischemic stroke. These findings suggest that NfL levels in the hyperacute stroke setting may reflect acute ischemic injury but also pre-existing chronic microvascular brain damage, supporting consideration of WMH burden when interpreting neuroaxonal biomarkers after stroke.
title: White matter hyperintensity burden is associated with neuroaxonal injury in acute ischemic stroke.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is frequently performed in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR); however, the optimal timing of PCI remains uncertain, particularly in patients with frailty-related high-risk features. Evidence comparing pre-TAVR versus concomitant PCI strategies in this vulnerable population is limited.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network to identify patients with frailty-related high-risk features undergoing TAVR with either pre-TAVR PCI (3 months to 2 weeks before TAVR) or concomitant PCI (same day as TAVR). Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using demographics, comorbidities, frailty-related features, and antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy. The primary outcome was a 90-day composite including all-cause mortality, acute kidney injury, bleeding requiring transfusion, gastrointestinal bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, acute coronary syndrome, and ischemic stroke. Secondary outcomes included the composite outcome at 30 days and 1 year, as well as individual components.
RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 361 patients were included in each group with adequate baseline balance. The primary 90-day composite outcome occurred in 27.4% of patients undergoing pre-TAVR PCI and 29.4% undergoing concomitant PCI (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.85-1.35; p=0.56). At 30 days, the composite outcome occurred in 21.9% and 24.4% of patients, respectively (RR 1.11, 95% CI 0.85-1.45; p=0.43). At 1 year, the composite outcome occurred in 37.1% of the pre-TAVR PCI group and 38.5% of the concomitant PCI group (RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.86-1.25; p=0.70). No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality at any time point.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with frailty-related high-risk features undergoing TAVR, pre-TAVR PCI and concomitant PCI were associated with similar short- and longer-term clinical outcomes. No significant differences were observed in the 90-day composite outcome or all-cause mortality. These findings support an individualized approach to PCI timing in frail, high-risk patients.
title: A Propensity-Matched Analysis of Pre Versus Concomitant Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With Frailty-Related High-Risk Features.

abstract:
AIMS: Current guidelines recommend targeting systolic blood pressure (SBP) below 130 mmHg in patients at high cardiovascular risk, including after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), although evidence specific to the post-ACS setting remains limited. We evaluated the prognostic value of SBP measured 1 year after ACS on subsequent cardiovascular outcomes.
METHODS: The ELIPS cohort prospectively enrolled ACS patients across four Swiss tertiary-care centers (2009-2017). Patients alive at 1 year with available SBP measurements were included. The association between SBP at 1 year and 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; cardiovascular death, non-fatal stroke/transient ischemic attack, or non-fatal myocardial infarction) was modeled using restricted cubic splines, adjusted for age, sex, renal function, cardiovascular risk factors, index-event type, coronary revascularization, cardiac rehabilitation, heart-failure history, and antihypertensive medication classes.
RESULTS: Among 2,074 patients (age 63±12 years; 82% male; 53% STEMI), 229 MACE events occurred over a median follow-up of 4.0 years (2.7 per 100 patient-years). The SBP-MACE relationship was nonlinear and J-shaped (P-non-linearity=0.007), with lowest risk between ∼130 and 140 mmHg (formally estimated nadir 138 mmHg [95%CI 116-152]). Above 140 mmHg, each 5-mmHg increase was associated with a borderline increase in MACE risk (adjusted HR 1.08; 95%CI 1.00-1.17). The pattern was broadly consistent across sex, age and hypertension status, with a possible interaction with diabetes that could not be excluded (P-interaction=0.08).
CONCLUSIONS: In this large, predominantly male, well-characterized post-ACS cohort, SBP measured 1 year after ACS showed a J-shaped association with cardiovascular risk, with lowest risk at 130-140 mmHg.
title: One-Year Systolic Blood Pressure and Subsequent Cardiovascular Outcomes After Acute Coronary Syndrome: Insights from a Swiss Prospective Cohort.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coronary intravascular lithotripsy (CIVL) has emerged as a promising technique for modifying severe coronary calcification before stent deployment, yet real-world data are still limited. The present study aimed to evaluate the indications, procedural modalities, and clinical outcomes of CIVL in consecutive real-world patients.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of all patients in whom CIVL was attempted between April 2022 and December 2023 at our centre, representing our initial experience with this technique. Demographic, clinical, and procedural data were extracted from electronic medical records. Follow-up data were obtained via telephone contact in patients who survived the index hospitalization without major complications.
RESULTS: Seventy patients (mean age 76.9±9.3 years, 78.6% male) with one lesion per patient were included. The most frequent cardiovascular risk factor was hypertension (65.7%). 52.9% of patients presented with acute coronary syndromes; and 25% with chronic coronary syndromes. The mean procedural time was 65.6±28.1minutes, fluoroscopy time 25.7±13.6minutes, and contrast volume 170.3±71.6mL. The left anterior descending artery (44.3%) and right coronary artery (34.3%) were most commonly treated. Proximal lesions constituted 42.9% of the cohort. The mean lithotripsy balloon diameter was 3.3±0.5mm; mean stent diameter 3.4±0.5mm; average number of stents per lesion 1.5±0.7; and total stent length 34.6±18.6mm. In 8.3% of cases, CIVL was used as a bailout strategy for stent underexpansion. Angiographic success was achieved in 92.9% of procedures; one case (1.4%) resulted in coronary perforation. In 5.7% of lesions, the operator could not cross the lesion with the balloon; 2.9% required adjunctive rotational atherectomy. Over follow-up, cardiovascular death occurred in 7.1%, with no documented myocardial infarction, stroke, or target vessel revascularization.
CONCLUSION: In an older, comorbid population, CIVL appears to be an effective and safe strategy for treating heavily calcified coronary lesions, with a high angiographic success rate and acceptable complications. Our findings demonstrate that CIVL can be rapidly and safely integrated into the routine clinical workflow of a regional center, even in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome.
title: Treatment of calcified coronary lesions with intravascular lithotripsy: experience of a regional French centre.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a causal risk factor for coronary artery disease, but its relationship with coronary plaque morphology assessed by optical coherence tomography (OCT) remains incompletely characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between circulating Lp(a) levels and OCT-defined coronary plaque phenotypes using a comprehensive segment-level approach.
METHODS: In this prospective single-center study (RELACS registry; NCT05496790), consecutive patients undergoing intracoronary OCT with available Lp(a) measurements were included. Coronary vessels were divided into 3 mm segments and analyzed for plaque characteristics. Lp(a) was primarily modeled as a continuous variable to assess its association with OCT-defined plaque phenotypes, including high-risk, layered, and fibrous plaques. High-risk plaque was defined as the presence of ≥2 criteria between lipid-rich plaque, thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA), and macrophages. Mixed-effects logistic regression models were used to account for within-patient clustering.
RESULTS: A total of 952 coronary segments from 50 patients were analyzed. Increasing Lp(a) levels were significantly associated with multiple features of plaque vulnerability, including TCFA, lipid-rich plaques, macrophages, and microchannels. In the multivariate mixed-effects analysis, higher Lp(a) levels were independently associated with a greater likelihood of high-risk plaque (odds ratios [OR] 1.31, 95% CI 1.16-1.48; P < .001) and layered plaques (OR 1.15, 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .024), whereas an inverse association was observed with fibrous plaques (OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.70-1.00; P = .047).
CONCLUSION: Increasing Lp(a) levels were associated with OCT-defined coronary plaque phenotypes related to vulnerability and instability, including high-risk and layered plaques. Given the limited patient-level sample size, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.
title: "Lipoprotein(a) across coronary plaque phenotypes from high-risk to layered plaque: An OCT analysis from the RELACS registry".

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal extracranial management in acute ischemic stroke due to tandem occlusions remains controversial. Balloon-expandable stents used as a bridging strategy with reduced early antiplatelet therapy have been proposed to decrease hemorrhagic risk, but comparative real-world data remain limited.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 268 consecutive patients with tandem occlusions treated with mechanical thrombectomy and one of three extracranial reconstruction strategies: percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA, n = 63), balloon-mounted coronary stenting as bridging therapy (n = 56), or self-expanding carotid stenting (n = 149). The primary endpoint was symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH). Secondary endpoints included hemorrhagic subtypes, reperfusion metrics, re-occlusion, and 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS]).
RESULTS: Baseline stroke severity differed among groups, with higher NIHSS scores and larger infarct core volumes in the balloon-expandable stent group (p = 0.001). Early antiplatelet therapy within 24 h also differed significantly among treatment strategies (p < 0.001). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 10.1% of patients and did not differ among groups (p = 0.598). Rates of any hemorrhage (p = 0.071), hemorrhagic transformation (p = 0.377), PH1 (p = 0.651), and PH2 (p = 0.813) were comparable, although HT2 was more frequent in the balloon-expandable stent group (p = 0.018). Complete reperfusion (TICI 3) differed significantly among groups (p < 0.001). Favorable functional outcome (mRS 0-2) at 90 days was highest in the self-expanding stent group (71.1%) compared with PTA (47.6%) and balloon-expandable stenting (58.9%) (p = 0.004). However, after multivariable adjustment, favorable outcome was independently associated with younger age, lower baseline NIHSS, higher ASPECTS, and complete reperfusion, whereas extracranial treatment strategy was not independently associated with outcome. Re-occlusion rates did not differ among groups (p = 0.250).
CONCLUSIONS: Extracranial reconstruction strategy was not associated with differences in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage despite substantial variability in early antiplatelet therapy. Although favorable functional outcomes differed among treatment groups in unadjusted analyses, extracranial treatment strategy was not independently associated with outcome after multivariable adjustment. Hemorrhagic and functional outcomes in tandem occlusions appear to be driven primarily by baseline stroke severity, infarct burden, and reperfusion success, supporting an individualized approach to extracranial reconstruction.
title: Extracranial reconstruction strategies for management of acute tandem occlusion strokes: hemorrhage risks and functional outcome.
