abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the clinical relevance of right ventricular (RV) function assessed on echocardiography, its predictive utility for patients receiving mitral valve surgery remains uncertain. The primary objectives of this study were to characterize RV function before and after valvular surgery and to establish the diagnostic value of this assessment.
METHODS: Echocardiograms were collected prospectively from patients undergoing mitral valve surgery between 2020 and 2023. Subsequently, a retrospective analysis of preoperative and postoperative echocardiographic parameters was performed to evaluate RV function, including tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S'TDI), RV fractional area change (FAC), RV free wall longitudinal strain (RVFWLS), RV global longitudinal strain (RVGLS), and three-dimensional RV ejection fraction (3D RVEF). The study included 115 patients with mitral valve surgery. Serial echocardiographic evaluations were performed at four time points: preoperatively, 1 week postoperatively, 6 months postoperatively, and 1 year postoperatively. Serial changes in echocardiographic parameters (TAPSE, FAC, S'TDI, RVFWLS, and 3D‑RVEF) were analyzed via repeated‑measures analysis of variance (ANOVA). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and DeLong tests were used to evaluate and compare diagnostic performance. Reproducibility for RVFWLS, RVGLS, and 3D‑RVEF was assessed according to intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland-Altman plots in a random subset of 20 observations.
RESULTS: The principal findings were as follows: (I) RV systolic function demonstrated a statistically significant reduction postoperatively as compared to the preoperative baseline level (P<0.0001). (II) One year after operation, TAPSE and S'TDI remained significantly lower than their corresponding preoperative values, with mean changes of -0.34 mm [95% confidence interval (CI): -0.55 to -0.14; P=0.0003] and 1.48 cm/s (95% CI: 0.45 to 2.52; P=0.0024), respectively. In contrast, RVFWLS and 3D RVEF recovered to levels comparable to those at baseline, with mean changes of 0.29% (95% CI: -2.19% to 2.77%; P>0.05) and -3.04% (95% CI: -9.98% to 3.91%; P>0.05), respectively. (III) According to the DeLong test, RVFWLS demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for RV systolic dysfunction (area under the curve =0.771), significantly outperforming conventional parameters (FAC, TAPSE, and S'TDI; all P values <0.001). (IV) RVFWLS exhibited stronger diagnostic agreement with the reference standard (3D RVEF) in identifying impaired RV systolic function, as indicated by the reclassification rate (31%), as compared to conventional parameters (57-64%).
CONCLUSIONS: RVFWLS may serve as a novel indicator for assessing RV systolic function both preoperatively and postoperatively in patients with mitral regurgitation (MR).
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: Serial changes in right ventricular function after mitral valve surgery: retrospective analysis of a prospective cohort.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) has emerged as a novel technology for modifying calcified coronary lesions, whereas optical coherence tomography (OCT) enables high-resolution assessment of calcium modification and procedural outcomes. However, the mechanistic and procedural effects of IVL assessed by OCT across studies remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261332946). PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, and Epistemonikos were searched from inception through February 2026. Randomized controlled trials and observational studies with extractable quantitative OCT outcomes were included. The primary endpoint was OCT-detected calcium fracture. Secondary endpoints included multiple calcium fractures, minimum stent area (MSA), stent expansion, acute lumen gain, procedural success, and in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to estimate pooled proportions or mean values with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Thirty studies encompassing a total of 3030 patients were included. OCT-detected calcium fracture occurred in 68% (95% CI 56%-79%) of lesions, whereas multiple fractures were observed in 34% (95% CI 26%-41%). IVL-treated lesions achieved favorable procedural metrics, including a pooled final MSA of 6.45 (95% CI 6.07-6.82) mm2, stent expansion of 85.9% (95% CI 82.3%-89.5%), and acute lumen gain of 3.50 (95% CI 3.14-3.87) mm2. Procedural success was high (95%, 95% CI 93%-98%) with low in-hospital MACEs (2%, 95% CI 1%-3%). Substantial heterogeneity was observed across endpoints.
CONCLUSIONS: Coronary IVL assessed by OCT is frequently associated with calcium fracture and favorable procedural outcomes with high procedural success and low early adverse events.
title: Optical Coherence Tomography Findings Following Intravascular Lithotripsy in Calcified Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathologic Q waves on the admission electrocardiogram (ECG) have historically been markers of myocardial necrosis and adverse outcomes after ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Although quantitative markers such as Q-wave width may add prognostic value, they can be difficult to apply clinically. We hypothesised that maximal and average pre-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) Q-wave depth could predict short- and medium-term mortality.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI (N = 625). Pre-PCI ECGs were analysed using European Society of Cardiology/American Heart Association definitions to identify pathologic Q waves. Maximal and average Q-wave depth (mm) and infarct territory were recorded. Posterior patterns, bundle branch block confounding interpretation, and Q waves outside the culprit territory were excluded. Outcomes were all-cause mortality at 3 and 12 months.
RESULTS: Of the 625 patients studied, 203 with pathologic Q waves in the infarct territory had complete depth measurements for analysis. Twelve-month mortality was 7.4% (15 of 203). Neither maximal nor average Q-wave depth was associated with mortality at 3 or 12 months in any infarct territory. Pain-to-balloon time demonstrated a weak positive correlation with maximal (Spearman rho = 0.204, P = 0.004) and average (rho = 0.152, P = 0.033) Q-wave depth.
CONCLUSIONS: In this small, observational cohort of STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, preprocedural Q-wave depth was not associated with all-cause mortality at 3 or 12 months. These findings do not support Q-wave depth as a standalone pre-PCI prognostic marker; larger studies and alternative ECG measures may be more informative. Q-wave depth was weakly associated with total ischemic time, warranting further evaluation in larger multicentre cohorts.
title: Preprocedural Q-wave Depth Does Not Predict Mortality After Primary Coronary Intervention for ST-elevation Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) is a significant risk factor for myocardial infarction (MI), adversely affecting left ventricular (LV) structure and function and worsening clinical outcomes. Given the interaction between ventricles, the right heart may also be affected by MI. This study investigated the additional effects of HTG on right ventricular (RV) deformation in patients with acute MI.
METHODS: The study included 101 patients with MI [58 without HTG (HTG-) and 43 with HTG (HTG+)] and 83 control participants, all of whom underwent cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. The patients with MI were categorized into HTG+ and HTG- subgroups. RV and LV function and strain were assessed, and multivariate linear regression was performed to identify determinants of RV peak strain (PS).
RESULTS: Compared with the HTG- group, the HTG+ group exhibited higher total cholesterol and troponin levels (P=0.002 and P=0.043, respectively), as well as significantly lower RV radial, circumferential, and longitudinal PS (all P<0.05 after Bonferroni correction). RV radial PS was inversely correlated with LV mass (r=-0.349, P=0.021), total cholesterol (r=-0.402, P=0.007), troponin (r=-0.584, P<0.001), and infarct size (r=-0.410, P=0.006). RV circumferential PS was correlated with multiple LV parameters, lipids, and infarct extent (r=0.323 to 0.574; all P<0.05). After adjusting for age, sex, and blood pressure, HTG remained independently associated with impaired RV radial, circumferential, and longitudinal PS (all P<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: HTG is associated with greater RV strain impairment in patients with MI. Our findings suggest that triglyceride levels and LV infarct extent may be associated with RV strain impairment, warranting further investigation in prospective studies.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: Impact of hypertriglyceridemia on right ventricular deformation in patients with left ventricular myocardial infarction: a cardiac magnetic resonance imaging study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Given the paradigm shift from surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) to transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for severe aortic stenosis (AS), we examined the temporal trends in AS hospitalization and treatment across Canada.
METHODS: Data from the Canadian Institute for Health Information Discharge Abstract Database were used for a population-based cross-sectional study of inpatients between April 1, 2012, and March 31, 2024. We estimated national and provincial rates and reported the annual changes in hospitalization for AS, SAVR, and TAVI. Rates were expressed as episodes/procedures per million, and stratified by age group, sex, and urban-vs-rural residence.
RESULTS: Between 2012 and 2024, hospitalizations for AS increased from 259.8 to 362.4 per million. Rates of SAVR declined from 104.4 to 66.5 per million, whereas rates of TAVI rose from 19.0 to 136.9 per million. The average annual per-million increases in AS hospitalizations were highest in Prince Edward Island (25.0), Nova Scotia (22.9), and Newfoundland and Labrador (21.3), particularly among individuals ≥ 80 years of age. The rates of SAVR declined, as the uptake of TAVI increased, with the shift mostly evident in those 60-79 years of age. Rates of TAVI were higher in men than in women, whereas AS hospitalizations were higher in rural than in urban areas.
CONCLUSIONS: Not unexpectedly there has been a dramatic shift from SAVR to TAVI observed, with an overall improvement in access to care. Nevertheless, sex-related and geographic disparities persist, highlighting the need for a coordinated national effort to ensure equitable access to AS management.
title: Temporal Trends in Hospitalization and Interventions for Aortic Stenosis in Canada, 2012-2024.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Natural language processing can transform unstructured clinical data into actionable insights that optimize workflows, improve patient outcomes, and reduce bias. We created a machine learning model that predicted suspicion of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) based on physician notes and assessed its capability to predict major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) when implemented within the HEART (history, electrocardiogram, age, risk factors, troponin) score.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed adults presenting with chest pain to The Ottawa Hospital emergency departments (EDs). GPT-4 produced and extracted 11 binary symptom features from physician-documented history of present illness. An extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) classifier was trained on these features to predict ED disposition, a surrogate marker of physician suspicion of ACS (pACS). The resulting natural language processing-derived ACS suspicion score (nACS) replaced the history component of HEART (nHEART) and was compared with the disposition-based composite (pHEART).
RESULTS: Of 1011 patients (48.5% female; mean age, 55.7 years), 69 (6.8%) experienced MACE within 6 weeks. nHEART achieved sensitivity of 97.1% and specificity of 53.8%; pHEART achieved sensitivity and specificity of 95.7% and 69.1%, respectively. pACS and troponin were the strongest multivariable predictors. GPT-4o extraction showed Fleiss' kappa > 0.8 across runs and Cohen's kappa > 0.6 vs extraction by research assistants.
CONCLUSIONS: Large language models can extract structured symptom features from ED notes, and an XGBoost model trained on these features can reproduce a coarse measure of physician suspicion of ACS. Clinical deployment will require further model training and testing against a prospectively documented measure of physician ACS suspicion.
title: Natural Language Processing for Risk Stratification of Emergency Department Patients with Chest Pain.
Real-World Yield of the RAISE Score for Cardiac Amyloidosis Screening in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract: This scoping review aims to consolidate the current evidence on the use of machine learning (ML) algorithms to predict mortality following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) procedures. This review was conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) guidelines. Electronic databases, including Medline, Embase, Cochrane, and ClinicalTrials.gov, were searched for studies assessing the use of ML models for the prediction of mortality in patients undergoing TAVR. A total of 1076 citations were screened, of which 21 studies underwent full-text review. Ultimately, 11 studies comprising 101,030 patients were included for data extraction. Study sample sizes ranged from 178 to 54,739 patients, with reported mortality intervals ranging from 30 days to 5 years after surgery. The parameters that were included in these ML models included demographic and clinical variables, electrocardiographic findings, laboratory results, computed tomography scans, and the type and size of the selected TAVR device. A total of 13 ML models were assessed across the included studies. Random Forest appeared to be the highest performing ML model in predicting 30-day and 1-year survival following TAVR, with reported area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) scores ranging from 0.66 to 0.97. In addition, the gradient-boosted machine seemed to outperform the CoreValve and TAVI2-SCORE in predicting 1-year survival. ML models may allow for accurate prediction of mortality following TAVR and may offer advantages over traditional clinical risk scores. However, limited datasets and variability in algorithm metric scores remain the main limitations to the implementation of these models in clinical practice.
title: Machine Learning for Predicting Mortality Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Scoping Review of Current Literature.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following acute coronary syndrome (ACS) treated by percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), guideline-directed dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) typically consists of 12 months of aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor. Recent trials support antiplatelet de-escalation strategies in patients at high bleeding risk (HBR), whereas patients undergoing complex PCI are at increased thrombotic risk and may benefit from extended DAPT. The overlap between these groups with high bleeding risk and high thrombotic risk in contemporary practice is not well characterized.
METHODS: Patients undergoing PCI for ACS were randomly sampled from those hospitalized at the Montreal Heart Institute between May 1, 2024 and April 30, 2025. Data were extracted from electronic health records. HBR was assessed using the Predicting Bleeding Complications in Patients Undergoing Stent Implantation and Subsequent Dual Antiplatelet Therapy-High Bleeding Risk (PRECISE-HBR) score, and complex PCI was assessed using guideline-based criteria. The primary objective was to estimate the proportion of patients meeting both criteria; secondary objectives described discharge antiplatelet strategies across risk groups.
RESULTS: Of the 309 participants sampled, 35% were identified as being at HBR, 43% underwent complex PCI, and 17.5% (95% confidence interval, 13.3%-21.7%) met both HBR and complex PCI criteria. De-escalation strategies were infrequently prescribed across risk groups, even among patients at HBR without complex PCI. Among those not receiving long-term anticoagulation, only 4.2% received a de-escalation strategy.
CONCLUSIONS: Nearly 1 in 6 patients undergoing PCI for ACS met both HBR and complex PCI criteria. In this setting, clinicians appeared to favour standard-duration clopidogrel-based DAPT rather than de-escalation approaches. These findings underscore the need for practical guidance to support individualized antiplatelet decision-making in patients with competing bleeding and ischemic risks.
title: Antiplatelet Therapy Strategies in Patients with High Bleeding Risk Treated with Complex Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Descriptive Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Internally stented (IS) surgical valves, such as Mitroflow (Sorin Group, Arvada, CO) and Trifecta (St. Jude Medical), are known to carry an elevated risk for coronary artery obstruction during valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) procedures. The data from comparison between balloon-expandable valves (BEVs) and supra-annular self-expanding valves (SEVs) for ViV-TAVI within the IS valve remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate clinical and hemodynamic outcomes of using BEVs and SEVs for TAVI within an IS valve.
METHODS: Between January 2016 and February 2024, propensity score-matching was performed between BEV and SEV groups in patients undergoing ViV-TAVI within an IS valve. The data of baseline characteristics, hemodynamic parameters, and clinical outcomes were retrospectively collected. Primary endpoints were 30-day and 2-year clinical outcomes, including all-cause death, hospitalization for heart failure, and coronary obstruction.
RESULTS: In total, 113 patients were included in this analysis. A total of 63 patients (55.8%) underwent BEV implantation, and 50 patients (44.2%) underwent SEV implantation. Overall, 37 pairs were identified after propensity-score matching. At day 30, the clinical and hemodynamic outcomes were similar between the groups. Patients with an SEV had better post-procedural mean gradient at 1 year compared with those with a BEV (11.7 ± 4.3 mm Hg vs 22.7 ± 8.4 mm Hg; P < 0.001). No significant difference was observed between SEVs and BEVs in the cumulative 2-year composite endpoint (log-rank P = 0.489).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients who underwent ViV within an IS valve, the early- and midterm clinical outcomes were comparable between BEVs and SEVs. However, use of an SEV was associated with superior hemodynamics at 1-year follow-up, vs a BEV.
title: Balloon-Expandable Vs Self-Expanding Valves for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Internally Stented Surgical Valves.
In-Stent Restenosis in Transition: Interpreting the Rise of Adjunctive Therapy.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical practice guidelines recommend the use of clopidogrel among patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. The frequency of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, such as ticagrelor or prasugrel, in this setting is not well known.
METHODS: Using the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI registry, we analyzed patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention from April 2018 to June 2024, excluding those discharged on oral anticoagulants. Temporal trends in high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription were examined. A mixed-effects multivariable logistic regression model with a random intercept for hospital was used to identify patient-, procedural-, and institutional-level factors associated with high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription while accounting for within-hospital clustering. Between-hospital variation was quantified using the median odds ratio.
RESULTS: Among 783 977 patients across 1815 hospitals, 35% were prescribed a high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor at discharge. The use of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors declined from 35% in 2018 to 31% in 2024 (P-trend=0.019), driven by a reduction in ticagrelor (from 29% to 23%, P-trend <0.001) despite a modest increase in prasugrel use (from 6.2% to 8%, P-trend=0.10). Male sex, prior myocardial infarction, and markers of procedural complexity (high-complexity/type C lesions, left main coronary artery, proximal left anterior descending artery, or use of mechanical circulatory support) were associated with higher odds of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription. In contrast, older age (≥75 years), prior stroke/transient ischemic attack, prior coronary artery bypass graft, severe renal dysfunction, and chronic total occlusion were associated with lower odds. University hospitals had lower odds of prescribing high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, with considerable variability in prescription patterns among institutions (median odds ratio, 2.59).
CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one-third of chronic coronary syndrome patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention were discharged on high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, with decreasing trends over time. Practice patterns reflected perceived ischemic versus bleeding risk and significant institutional variation, underscoring opportunities for quality improvement and guideline alignment.
title: High-Potency P2Y12 Inhibitors Among Patients With Chronic Coronary Syndrome Undergoing PCI: An Analysis From the NCDR CathPCI Registry.

abstract: Evolocumab is a monoclonal antibody targeting PCSK9 that provides rapid and sustained LDL-cholesterol reduction. Following FOURIER, which demon-strated a reduction in cardiovascular events in patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, VESALIUS-CV extends this benefit to high- or very-high-risk patients without previous myocardial infarction or stroke. These findings support earlier, intensive and sustained LDL-cholesterol lowering. This review summarizes the main evidence supporting evolocumab across the cardiovascular risk continuum.
title: [Evolocumab (Repatha®) : new evidence across the continuum of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease].

abstract: ObjectiveTo determine whether rapid intracoronary adenosine administration attenuates percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)-induced systemic inflammation and oxidative stress in patients with coronary artery disease.MethodsThis prospective, randomized controlled trial enrolled patients undergoing coronary angiography (coronary angiography group) or PCI. Patients undergoing PCI were assigned to receive intracoronary adenosine (PCI + adenosine group) or placebo (PCI group). Blood levels of inflammatory markers (e.g. cytokines), anti-inflammatory mediators, and oxidative stress indicators (superoxide dismutase and malondialdehyde) were measured before and 24 h after the procedure.ResultsCompared to the coronary angiography group, patients undergoing PCI who received placebo exhibited concurrent elevations in inflammatory and anti-inflammatory markers at 24 h. Intracoronary adenosine significantly suppressed the rise in the levels of inflammatory markers (e.g. interleukin-6 reduced by 35% vs. placebo) and enhanced anti-inflammatory responses (e.g. interleukin-10 increased by 40% vs. placebo). Following PCI, oxidative stress was evident in placebo-treated patients, as reflected by decreased superoxide dismutase activity (15% reduction) and increased malondialdehyde levels (30% elevation). Adenosine restored superoxide dismutase activity to near-baseline levels and reduced malondialdehyde elevation by 85% compared to placebo.ConclusionsIntracoronary adenosine mitigates PCI-associated systemic inflammation and oxidative stress by rebalancing inflammatory pathways and preserving redox homeostasis. These findings highlight its potential as a therapeutic adjunct for improving clinical outcomes following PCI and warrant further validation in large-scale trials.Clinical Trial Registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR); identifier: ChiCTR1800019349.
journal: The Journal of international medical research
title: Effects of adenosine on oxidative stress and inflammation in patients with coronary heart disease underlying percutaneous coronary intervention.

abstract: IntroductionEvidence surrounding the optimal antithrombotic regimen for patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) requiring oral anticoagulation remains scarce. This meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy and safety of oral anticoagulant (OAC) monotherapy compared to OAC plus single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) in this population.MethodsWe systematically searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) till February 2026 comparing OAC monotherapy versus OAC plus SAPT in patients with CCS. Primary outcomes included major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding, net adverse clinical events (NACE), all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular (CV) deaths. Pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated.ResultsOAC monotherapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding compared with dual antithrombotic therapy (DAT) (RR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.38-0.65; p < 0.001; I2 = 42%). Similarly, OAC monotherapy significantly reduced the incidence of NACE (RR: 0.64; 95% CI: 0.50-0.81; p < 0.001; I2 = 64%). There was no significant difference between the two strategies in all-cause mortality (RR: 0.79; 95% CI: 0.55-1.13; p = 0.20; I2 = 52%). However, OAC monotherapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of CV mortality (RR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.53-0.97; p = 0.03; I2 = 3%).ConclusionIn patients with CCS requiring long-term oral anticoagulation, OAC monotherapy significantly reduced major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding, CV mortality, and NACE compared with dual antithrombotic therapy (DAT). Rates of major ischemic events, Myocardial Infarction, stroke, and all-cause mortality were comparable between the two strategies.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCTs comparing OAC monotherapy with OAC plus SAPT in chronic coronary syndrome; the abstract does not give the number of trials or patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not state the number of trials, and heterogeneity was moderate to substantial for some outcomes (I2 = 64% for NACE).
appraisal.one_line: A meta-analysis of randomised trials found less bleeding with oral anticoagulant monotherapy than with anticoagulant plus single antiplatelet therapy in chronic coronary syndrome.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: OAC monotherapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding compared with dual antithrombotic therapy (DAT) (RR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.38-0.65; p < 0.001; I2 = 42%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Antithrombotic de-escalation in anticoagulated patients with stable coronary disease is a common decision.

journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
title: Oral Anticoagulant Monotherapy vs. Combination Therapy in Chronic Coronary Syndrome Requiring Long-Term Anticoagulation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

abstract:
PURPOSE: Bladder neck contracture (BNC) following anatomical endoscopic enucleation of the prostate (AEEP) occurs in approximately 3% of cases and carries high recurrence rates after standard endoscopic management. The Optilume drug-coated balloon (DCB) delivers paclitaxel at dilation but has not been reported for post-enucleation BNC. We describe the first such series following pulsed thulium laser enucleation of the prostate (p-ThuLEP).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 10 consecutive patients with cystoscopically confirmed BNC after p-ThuLEP at a single high-volume center (IRB 2425566-1). All underwent laser enucleation of bladder neck scar followed by Optilume DCB dilation. Data were abstracted from the electronic health record.
RESULTS: Median age was 74 years (range 59-89). Median pre-p-ThuLEP prostate volume was 80 cc (range 36-100, n = 8). BNC presented at a median of 5.8 months after p-ThuLEP (range 2.7-12.0). A 36F balloon was used in nine patients and a 26F balloon in one, at 8 to 11 atm for 5 minutes. At a median follow-up of 5.2 months (range 0.9-15.1), no patient required reintervention (0% recurrence). Cystoscopy, performed in 5 of 10 on clinical indication, showed a patent bladder neck in all. Median post-procedure Qmax was 14.1 mL/s (n = 7), and post-void residual was 23.5 mL (n = 10). Thirty-day complications after Optilume occurred in two patients (20%), both Clavien-Dindo Grade II: gross hematuria with clot retention managed by continuous bladder irrigation and urinary tract infection.
CONCLUSIONS: Optilume DCB following laser enucleation of post-p-ThuLEP BNC appears safe and feasible with encouraging short-term patency. Median follow-up (5.2 months) is shorter than the median interval to BNC presentation (5.8 months); thus, these short-term data do not establish durability. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first report of Optilume DCB outcomes for BNC specifically following AEEP. A prospective cohort trial with longer follow-up is warranted.
keywords: anatomic endoscopic enucleation of the prostate
title: Optilume Drug-Coated Balloon for Bladder Neck Contracture Following Pulsed Thulium:YAG Laser Enucleation of the Prostate: A Single-Institution Retrospective Case Series.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The operational definition and imaging assessment of the no-reflow phenomenon, a potential contributor to poor clinical outcome despite successful thrombectomy, remains debated. We aimed to develop expert-based international consensus on the definition, assessment, and reporting standard of cerebral no-reflow post-thrombectomy.
METHODS: Three-rounds of a modified Delphi web-based survey was conducted among corresponding authors of peer-reviewed clinical studies on cerebral no-reflow between 2020 and 2025. Responses at each round were used to develop structured questionnaires for subsequent rounds. Consensus was predefined as ≥65% agreement.
RESULTS: Among 27 panelists, the response rate was 70%, 74%, and 74% over all rounds. There was broad agreement to conceptualize no-reflow as macrovascular recanalization with impaired microvascular reperfusion. Consensus was reached that macrovascular recanalization is ideally assessed as (1) digital subtraction angiography with expanded thrombolysis in cerebral infarction (eTICI) grades 2c without clear distal vessel occlusions and/or eTICI 3 only, and (2) absence of a wedge-shaped time-to-maximum (Tmax) or time-to-peak (TTP) delay on post-recanalization perfusion computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Regarding impaired microvascular reperfusion assessment, cerebral blood flow, and/or volume were preferred over time-based perfusion parameters (Tmax/TTP). The panel expressed a preference that no-reflow should ideally be assessed ≤6 hours post-recanalization. Pending formal validation, histopathological-radiological correlation in animal models would sufficiently validate the use of imaging-based definitions in humans.
INTERPRETATION: Based on currently available literature and expert opinions, this Delphi study provides a framework for systematically reporting cerebral no-reflow after endovascular treatment (EVT). The variability in opinions regarding quantitative thresholds highlights priorities for future methodological standardization and validation studies. ANN NEUROL 2026.
title: Cerebral No-Reflow after Thrombectomy: International Delphi Consensus on Definition and Imaging Assessment.

abstract: BackgroundBioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, specifically surgical (SAVR) and transcatheter (TAVR), is among the most frequently performed cardiac interventions globally, yet anticoagulation strategies after implantation remain incompletely defined. Atrial fibrillation, notably prevalent pre- and post-operatively in these patients, substantially amplifies thromboembolic risk and complicates decision-making in an already elderly, frail, and comorbid population.ObjectivesTo critically evaluate current anticoagulation strategies after bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement across sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation in both SAVR and TAVR, and to identify evidence gaps and guideline inconsistencies.MethodsWe conducted a narrative review of major international guidelines (ESC/EACTS 2025, ACC/AHA 2020, and NICE 2021) and key clinical trials on antithrombotic therapy in valve replacement populations. Focus was placed on bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, with mechanical and non-aortic valves excluded.ResultsAspirin monotherapy is the most consistently supported strategy after bioprosthetic TAVR in sinus rhythm, though guidelines diverge on duration and recommendation strength. In atrial fibrillation, all three guidelines apply uniform CHA2DS2-VASc-based frameworks irrespective of AF phenotype, procedural context, or detection modality, reflecting lacking evidence rather than deliberate clinical judgement. No trial has enrolled patients specifically with new-onset post-procedural AF or stratified by AF subtype, and subclinical AF after bioprosthetic AVR remains entirely uncharacterised.ConclusionsGuideline divergence reflects a structurally inadequate evidence base rather than genuine clinical equipoise. Individualised decisions informed by procedure type, AF phenotype, frailty, and bleeding risk are required to guide clinical practice, alongside an adequately powered stratified randomised trial incorporating mandatory continuous rhythm monitoring.
keywords: surgical and transcatheter aortic valve replacement
title: Anticoagulation after transcatheter and surgical bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement: A narrative review.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Protruding left ventricular outflow tract calcification represents a high-risk anatomical feature for transcatheter aortic valve replacement, predisposing to paravalvular regurgitation (PVR), annular injury, and conduction disturbance.
CASE SUMMARY: We present 4 patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis and protruding left ventricular outflow tract calcific nodules treated with the Navitor self-expanding valve system. Despite uniformly hostile landing-zone anatomy, procedural success was achieved in all cases. Residual PVR ranged from trivial to mild-to-moderate, with no patient developing moderate-or-greater PVR. All patients demonstrated hemodynamic improvement and early symptomatic benefit.
CONCLUSIONS: Calcific morphology and nodule orientation, rather than calcium burden alone, may be key determinants of PVR following Navitor implantation in hostile landing-zone anatomy. These findings are hypothesis-generating; the observed pattern of adaptive cuff sealing requires verification in larger, preferably comparative studies before conclusions regarding device-specific sealing mechanisms can be drawn.
title: Adaptive Sealing in Protruding LVOT Calcification During TAVR: A 4-Patient Case Series.

abstract: The management of mitral valve (MV) and tricuspid valve (TV) regurgitation has undergone significant transformation during the past decade. This change has been driven by a growing understanding of the adverse clinical consequences of these conditions, particularly their strong association with heart failure progression, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality-and by the emergence of effective transcatheter options for valve intervention. Among these, transcatheter MV edge-to-edge repair and replacement and transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair and replacement have become important therapeutic tools that provide a less invasive alternative to surgery in appropriately selected patients. In this clinical practice update we aim to provide contemporary, evidence-based guidance for clinicians in the evaluation and management of patients with severe, symptomatic MV or TV regurgitation who might benefit from transcatheter intervention. Key topics include the clinical presentation of these valve lesions, the diagnostic evaluation with emphasis on multimodality imaging and hemodynamics, criteria for patient selection, and current data on procedural and long-term clinical outcomes. A central theme is the role of timely referral and structured assessment to avoid missed opportunities for intervention. Optimal outcomes require active engagement from referring physicians and close collaboration within a multidisciplinary heart team, including cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, imaging specialists, heart failure specialists, and nursing partners-to ensure careful patient selection, procedural planning, and comprehensive post-intervention follow-up. By integrating clinical judgement with guideline-based recommendations and procedural expertise, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair or transcatheter valve replacement can offer substantial symptomatic relief and improved quality of life for selected patients, while minimizing procedural risk and enhancing overall cardiovascular outcomes.

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice update from Canadian societies; the abstract gives no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not describe the evidence grading method.
appraisal.one_line: A Canadian clinical practice update on transcatheter mitral and tricuspid edge-to-edge repair and replacement.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It offers contemporary referral and patient-selection guidance across mitral and tricuspid transcatheter therapy.

title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Society of Cardiovascular Surgery/Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology Clinical Practice Update on Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Valve Intervention: Patient Evaluation and Management.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Due to its unique anatomical and functional characteristics, the retina represents a promising organ for the evaluation of systemic vascular diseases. Modern imaging techniques, particularly optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A), enable noninvasive and quantitative assessment of retinal microcirculation. The aim of this review is to present current findings on the significance of retinal biomarkers in cardiovascular diseases, with a focus on heart failure.
RESULTS: Numerous studies show associations between retinal vascular changes and arterial hypertension, coronary heart disease, left ventricular hypertrophy, and heart failure. Changes in retinal vascular parameters such as vascular density and perfusion density correlate with structural and functional cardiac changes. Patients with retinal vascular occlusions have an increased risk of stroke, myocardial infarction, and higher cardiovascular mortality. Initial studies in patients with acute decompensated heart failure have demonstrated changes in retinal vascular and perfusion density that can be reversed by recompensation. These observations led to the introduction of the term "cardio-ocular syndrome," which describes the interactions between cardiac function, systemic congestion, and retinal microcirculation.
CONCLUSION: Retinal imaging opens up new possibilities for the noninvasive assessment of systemic microcirculatory disorders in cardiovascular diseases. OCT‑A could contribute in the future to risk stratification, assessment of disease progression, and monitoring of therapy in heart failure.
title: [The eye as a mirror of the heart-retinal findings in heart failure and cardiovascular diseases].

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: The proliferation of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) facilities across the US has raised questions about whether expanding capacity improves outcomes in areas already served vs those without prior access.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between the opening of PCI-capable facilities and outcomes following acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in communities with and without baseline PCI access.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used California data from inpatient, emergency department, and ambulatory surgery encounters from January 1, 2011, to December 31, 2022, including all adults hospitalized with a primary diagnosis of AMI. Zip code communities were categorized by baseline (2011) access to PCI-capable facilities within a 30-minute drive.
EXPOSURE: Opening of a PCI-capable facility within 30 minutes of a community's zip code during the study period.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were (1) admission to a PCI-capable facility, (2) receipt of PCI during the index hospitalization, (3) unscheduled acute care visit within 30 days, and (4) all-cause mortality at 30 days and 1 year. Linear probability models with community and time-fixed effects estimated changes in outcomes following PCI facility openings separately for communities with and without baseline access.
RESULTS: Among 590 282 patients with AMI (157 435 younger than age 60 years [27%]; 222 773 female [38%]; 63 460 Asian [11%], 129 137 Hispanic [22%], 315 326 White [53%]), 500 778 (85%) lived in communities with baseline PCI access, and 89 504 (15%) lived in communities without; 18 805 patients (21%) without baseline access experienced a PCI opening. Openings in communities without baseline access were associated with a 30.0 percentage point (pp) increase (95% CI, 28.2 to 31.8 pp) in admission to PCI-capable hospitals and a 5.1 pp increase (95% CI, 3.3 to 7.0 pp) in PCI receipt, along with reductions in 30-day (-1.8 pp; 95% CI, -3.2 to -0.5 pp) and 1-year (-2.8 pp; 95% CI, -4.7 to -1.0 pp) mortality. In contrast, openings in communities with baseline access were associated with smaller gains in admission (1.5 pp; 95% CI, 1.1 to 1.9 pp), modest increases in PCI use (1.0 pp; 95% CI, 0.5 to 1.6 pp), decreases in unscheduled visits within 30 days (-0.7 pp; 95% CI, -1.2 to -0.2 pp), and no mortality change. Sensitivity analyses restricted to higher-volume PCI centers (50 annual cases or more) yielded consistent findings.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of 590 282 patients with AMI in California, opening new PCI facilities was associated with substantial improvements in communities without prior PCI availability, including a 53% relative increase in access to admission, 16% increase in PCI use, and 20% and 15% reductions in 30-day and 1-year mortality, respectively. In contrast, already served areas showed smaller benefits and no mortality improvement. PCI expansion should prioritize underserved regions to maximize population-level benefits and avoid inefficient duplication of services.

appraisal.main_limitation: Observational quasi-experimental design with possible unmeasured confounding.
appraisal.one_line: A cohort study using facility openings in California found that new PCI capacity in underserved communities was associated with lower mortality after AMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Openings in communities without baseline access were associated with a 30.0 percentage point (pp) increase (95% CI, 28.2 to 31.8 pp) in admission to PCI-capable hospitals and a 5.1 pp increase (95% CI, 3.3 to 7.0 pp) in PCI receipt, along with reductions in 30-day (-1.8 pp; 95% CI, -3.2 to -0.5 pp) and 1-year (-2.8 pp; 95% CI, -4.7 to -1.0 pp) mortality.

title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Facility Access and Clinical Outcomes Among Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a guideline-recommended secondary prevention program that reduces morbidity and mortality among patients with ischemic heart disease (IHD) yet remains underutilized. Over the past decade, the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) has implemented strategies to increase CR participation, including expansion of virtual home-based CR (HBCR) programs as alternatives to traditional center-based CR (CBCR).
OBJECTIVE: To examine temporal trends and factors associated with CR participation among veterans with IHD.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used national VHA electronic health record data to evaluate CR participation among veterans hospitalized for IHD, identified using International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision (ICD-9), ICD-10, or Current Procedural Terminology codes from 2012 to 2022. Data were analyzed from October 25, 2025, to July 25, 2026.
EXPOSURES: Availability of CR delivery models at Veterans Affairs (VA) facilities, including referral to community care programs only, VA CBCR, or VA HBCR.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the proportion of eligible veterans with acute myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass graft surgery who participated in any type of CR within 12 months of the index event, identified using Current Procedural Terminology codes and VA stop codes from VA-provided, VA-purchased, or Medicare-claimed services. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with CR participation.
RESULTS: Among 405 907 veterans with IHD (mean [SD] age, 68.5 [11.1] years; 391 998 men [96.6%]), 63 185 (15.6%) participated in CR. Participation increased from 9.6% in 2012 to 17.1% in 2022, with a peak of 19.7% in 2018. In 2022, participation was higher at facilities offering HBCR (20.0%) compared with those offering CBCR without HBCR (14.8%) or referral to community care programs only (14.3%). The adjusted odds ratio (AOR) of participation among veterans treated at facilities offering HBCR was 1.80 (95% CI, 1.75-1.84), whereas the AOR of participation at facilities offering CBCR without HBCR was 1.29 (95% CI, 1.26-1.32) compared with referral to community care programs only.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of veterans with IHD, participation in CR nearly doubled between 2012 and 2022. Patients who had index events at facilities offering HBCR had higher CR participation than those at facilities offering CBCR without HBCR, or at facilities offering only referral to community care. Broader availability of HBCR programs may help improve participation within large health systems.
mesh: United States Department of Veterans Affairs
title: Home-Based Programs and Cardiac Rehabilitation Participation Among Veterans With Ischemic Heart Disease.

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: One in 5 heart transplant candidates in the US die or are delisted without transplant. Donor hearts are currently allocated by a 6-status therapy-based system criticized for limited risk stratification and susceptibility to gaming.
OBJECTIVE: To develop a new heart allocation policy based on an objective medical urgency score that ranks candidates based on the interaction between physiology and mechanical circulatory support.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Registry-based observational study using data from the US organ transplant system. All adult (aged ≥18 years) heart transplant candidates from January 2019 to August 2025 were included, split into training (2019-2023), validation (2023-2024), and test (2024-2025) datasets.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: A marginal structural model of 6-week mortality without transplant was estimated (the US Candidate Risk Score [US-CRS]). Eight models were compared in held-out data by weighted time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and calibration by status. Finally, US-CRS was converted into an allocation policy and a match-run simulation of waitlist reordering was performed compared with the current 6-status system.
RESULTS: Adult heart transplant candidates were partitioned into consecutive training (n = 21 859), validation (n = 7897), and test (n = 8256) datasets (mean [SD] age, 53 [13] years; 74% male). The chosen US-CRS model included 5 laboratory values and 4 therapeutic devices (durable left ventricular assist device, intra-aortic balloon pump, microaxial flow pump, and advanced mechanical circulatory support). In test-set cross-sections of candidates actively waiting on the same calendar date, US-CRS had similar or significantly higher time-dependent AUC than the current 6-status system (mean AUC, 0.807 vs 0.693, respectively) and acceptable calibration by status, especially for candidates who received their status by exception. In match-run analysis (n = 45 530 donor hearts), a US-CRS-based system led to 67% of transplant recipients moving down in rank order and increased observed 6-week transplant-censored mortality for the first candidate on the match run from 11.2% (95% CI, 10.1%-12.5%) under the current system to 15.7% (95% CI, 13.9%-17.6%) under the US-CRS-based system.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this registry-based study of US heart transplant candidates, a US-CRS-based allocation system prioritized sicker candidates with higher mortality without transplant compared with the current medical urgency statuses.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry-based observational study; training (n = 21 859), validation (n = 7897) and test (n = 8256) datasets.
appraisal.main_limitation: Allocation performance rests on a simulation of waitlist reordering rather than prospective use.
appraisal.one_line: A registry-based score for US donor heart allocation that ranks candidates by medical urgency, including mechanical circulatory support.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: US-CRS had similar or significantly higher time-dependent AUC than the current 6-status system (mean AUC, 0.807 vs 0.693, respectively); first-candidate 6-week transplant-censored mortality was 11.2% (95% CI, 10.1%-12.5%) under the current system and 15.7% (95% CI, 13.9%-17.6%) under the US-CRS-based system.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Device-based urgency in advanced heart failure and shock bears on how mechanical support is used as a bridge.

title: Development and Validation of an Adult Medical Urgency Score for US Donor Heart Allocation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: In chronic total occlusion (CTO), donor vessels supplying collateral flow to the occluded artery may exhibit altered physiological indices, potentially influencing revascularization decisions. This case series evaluates the impact of successful CTO percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) on instantaneous wave-free ratio (iFR) measurements in donor vessels with moderate stenosis.
METHODS: We present a single-center case series (December 2020-September 2024) involving five patients with right coronary artery (RCA) CTO and a moderately diseased mid-left anterior descending artery (LAD) functioning as a collateral donor. All patients underwent ischemia testing and successful RCA CTO PCI. LAD iFR was measured before and after RCA revascularization.
RESULTS: Pre-PCI LAD iFR values ranged from 0.73 to 0.89, at or below the ischemic threshold. Post-RCA-PCI iFR improved in all cases (range: 0.87-0.96): in case 1, from 0.82 to 0.93; in case 2, from 0.82 to 0.89; in case 3, from 0.87 to 0.96; in case 4, from 0.73 to 0.87; and in case 5, from 0.89 to 0.96. In all cases, intervention on the LAD was deferred post-PCI, with no adverse clinical events during follow-up.
CONCLUSION: Successful RCA CTO PCI leads to immediate improvement in donor vessel iFR, suggesting that collateral demand may exaggerate ischemia. Staged physiologic assessment may improve decision-making in patients with moderate lesions in donor vessels.
title: The impact of chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention on the coronary physiology of the donor epicardial vessel: a case series.

abstract:
CONTEXT: Mean arterial pressure targets during cardiopulmonary bypass remain debated; vasopressor-driven pressure augmentation may not improve oxygen delivery.
AIMS: The aim of the paper is to describe clinical outcomes and physiologic markers during normothermic cardiopulmonary bypass managed with indexed flow, cerebral oximetry, calculated indexed oxygen delivery (DO2i), and vasopressor-sparing pressure management.
SETTINGS AND DESIGN: Single-center retrospective descriptive cohort study at a cardiac surgery center.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Consecutive adults undergoing elective or urgent cardiac surgery with normothermic cardiopulmonary bypass from June 2023 to December 2025 were included if complete anesthesia-perfusion, regional cerebral oxygen saturation (rSO2), circuit-derived venous oxygen saturation (SvO2), DO2i, and early outcome data were available. Circulatory arrest was excluded. Indexed pump flow was 2.2-2.4 L/min/m². Mean arterial pressure was interpreted with indexed flow, rSO2, SvO2, DO2i, hemoglobin, acid-base status, venous return, and surgical context. Baseline rSO2 was recorded before ventilation on room air; maximal relative decrease during bypass was recorded.
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED: Descriptive statistics and Wilson 95% confidence intervals were used. No comparative testing or causal modeling was performed.
RESULTS: Two hundred patients were analyzed. Operating-room extubation was achieved in 172 patients (86.0%). Stroke occurred in six (3.0%), acute kidney injury in two (1.0%), and venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was required in six (3.0%). Baseline right and left rSO2 were 57.5 ± 11.2% and 58.5 ± 11.3%; maximal relative rSO2 decrease was 28.5 ± 3.4%; circuit-derived SvO2 was 67.4 ± 5.9%; and calculated DO2i was 611 ± 74 mL/min/m².
CONCLUSIONS: This flow-oriented, cerebral oximetry-guided, oxygen-delivery-aware strategy was accompanied by favorable early recovery. Because the study was retrospective and noncomparative, the findings are hypothesis-generating.
title: Cerebral Oxygenation-Guided Indexed-Flow Normothermic Cardiopulmonary Bypass with Vasopressor-Sparing Pressure Management: A Retrospective Descriptive Cohort Study.

abstract: Coronary artery anomalies are rare but clinically significant malformations, particularly when involving an interarterial course, which predisposes to ischemia and sudden cardiac death. We report the case of a previously healthy 22-year-old man who suffered out-of-hospital cardiac arrest associated with recreational inhalant use. Imaging revealed an anomalous right coronary artery originating from the left sinus of Valsalva with interarterial trajectory. Surgical reimplantation was performed under tailored anesthetic management emphasizing hemodynamic stability. The patient recovered uneventfully. This case discusses and highlights anesthetic priorities and the potential role of external triggers in vulnerable coronary anatomy.
title: Anesthetic Challenges in Interarterial Right Coronary Artery Anomaly from the Left Sinus of Valsalva: A Case Report.

abstract: Uncorrected tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) can be associated with widespread abnormalities, but the giant right atrium (RA) is an extremely rare one. The giant RA can cause additional problems causing atrial arrythmias, thromboembolism, and compression of adjacent structures. Tricuspid regurgitation is common with annular dilatation. In symptomatic cases, reduction atrioplasty is recommended. Sternotomy should be careful to avoid damage to the giant RA. In asymptomatic cases, anticoagulation should be carried out. We report a rare case of uncorrected TOF associated with the giant RA and got successfully treated with surgery.
title: An Extremely Rare Association of the Giant Right Atrium with Uncorrected Tetralogy of Fallot in an Adolescent Male Patient.

abstract: Patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) often present acutely with decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic shock or cardiac arrest requiring immediate intervention. Treatment options for these patients include palliative care, balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV), emergency transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), or surgical aortic valve replacement. TAVI procedure is performed electively in majority of the patients. However, it can be considered a rescue therapy in patients with cardiogenic shock secondary to acutely decompensated valvular AS. Here, we report the successful use of emergent TAVI for a patient presenting with cardiogenic shock secondary to decompensated AS.
title: Emergency Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for Decompensated Aortic Stenosis accompanied by Cardiogenic Shock.

abstract: ObjectiveTo clinically validate the nursing diagnosis "Risk for shock" in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) admitted to an Intensive Care Unit (ICU).MethodA retrospective case-control study conducted at a high-complexity university hospital in Brazil. The sample consisted of 116 medical records of adult patients with AMI, equally distributed between the case group (with cardiogenic shock; n = 58) and the control group (without cardiogenic shock; n = 58). Diagnostic accuracy measures (sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and likelihood ratios) were calculated, and multivariate binary logistic regression using the Stepwise Forward method was applied to identify independent predictors and control for confounders.ResultsIn the accuracy analysis, the indicator "Unstable blood pressure" showed the best clinical balance, with a sensitivity of 85.0% (95% CI: 76.2-93.8) and a specificity of 83.6% (95% CI: 74.4-92.8). "Hyperthermia" and "Inadequate fluid volume" showed the highest individual specificities (90.1% and 80.3%, respectively). After adjusting the logistic regression model (Nagelkerke R2 = 0.614; Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.782), only four factors remained significant as independent predictors of the outcome: unstable blood pressure (aOR = 7.80; 95% CI: 3.10-19.60; p < 0.001), hypoxia (aOR = 3.70; 95% CI: 1.50-9.20; p = 0.006), hypoxemia (aOR = 2.90; 95% CI: 1.40-6.10; p = 0.004), and inadequate fluid volume (aOR = 2.10; 95% CI: 1.00-4.50; p = 0.048). Thermal and hemorrhagic indicators lost significance after adjustment.ConclusionThe study clinically validated the diagnosis and confirmed a robust predictive model composed of four indicators. Prioritizing the monitoring of these risk factors enables critical care nurses to anticipate hemodynamic collapse, support targeted care protocols, and optimize multiprofessional decision-making at the bedside.
title: Clinical Validation of the Nursing Diagnosis "Risk for Shock" in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction Admitted to the ICU.

abstract: Introduction After an acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or coronary revascularisation, the risk of recurrent vascular events remain substantial. Despite clear guideline recommendations, secondary prevention and long-term adherence to preventive treatment is often suboptimal. Current secondary prevention strategies typically involve initiating a limited number of pharmacologic therapies during hospitalisation, followed by sequential intensification after discharge to achieve individualized guideline-recommended targets. However, this strategy is prone to therapeutic inertia and negatively affects patient motivation and long-term adherence. We hypothesise that a 'first-time-right' strategy, where individualised, guideline-based pharmacological treatment is proactively initiated during hospitalisation, can improve risk factor control and adherence compared to current practice, and thereby reduce major cardiovascular events. Methods and analysis GOLDEN (Guided Optimisation for Long-term Disease rEduction in secoNdary Prevention of cardiovascular disease) is a prospective, temporally controlled observational cohort study aiming to include 5,586 patients hospitalised for ACS or coronary revascularisation. A guidelines-based 'first-time-right' pharmacological optimisation strategy will be compared to current practice on the 3-year incidence of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or ischemia-driven revascularisation (4-point MACE). This strategy targets both patients and healthcare professionals and aims to utilise the teachable moment during hospitalisation to optimise pharmacological strategies, apply key behavioural principles to improve adherence, and reframe follow-up from reactive up-titration to proactive de-escalation. A pocket card and online tool will be provided to check applicable guidelines during hospitalisation and formulate follow-up recommendations. An on-site training visit and communication aids are intended to support implementation and promote adherence. Summary This study will evaluate the effects of a 'first-time-right' strategy - focused on early in-hospital initiation and optimisation of guideline-based pharmacotherapy after acute coronary syndrome or coronary revascularisation - on the risk of recurrent MACE compared to current practice.
title: A 'First-Time-Right' strategy in secondary prevention of coronary artery disease: Rationale and design of the prospective, temporally controlled observational GOLDEN study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation is often limited by the significant risk of bleeding, and difficulties maintaining consistent adherence over time. These challenges have led to the development of left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) as an alternative stroke prevention strategy in this patient population. Our study aimed to evaluate LAAC versus medical therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation.
METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library from database inception through April 1, 2026. The predefined endpoints were composite outcome of systemic embolism, cardiovascular mortality, or stroke in addition to other endpoints including all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, strokes, and major bleeding. All outcomes were pooled using a random effect Mantel-Haenszel model. The between-study variance (τ2) was estimated using the Paul Mendel method, which is the preferred method when the number of included studies is small.
RESULTS: A total of five randomized controlled trials, 5,404 patients were analyzed; 2,878 underwent LAAC and 2,526 received medical therapy. The median follow-up across studies was 4 years. LAAC met noninferiority compared with medical therapy in atrial fibrillation for major bleeding (RR 0.86; 95% CI 0.59-1.26) and all-cause mortality (RR 0.93; 95% CI 0.71-1.22). In contrast, noninferiority was not met for the composite outcome (RR 0.97; 95% CI 0.64-1.47), cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.86; 95% CI 0.51-1.42), systemic embolism (RR 1.93; 95% CI 0.21-17.5), and all stroke (RR 1.11; 95% CI 0.73-1.67).
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis showed that LAAC was noninferior to anticoagulation for all-cause mortality and major bleeding, but it did not meet noninferiority for the other assessed outcomes, including stroke, cardiovascular mortality, and/or systemic embolism.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCTs; five randomized controlled trials, 5,404 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Noninferiority was not met for several efficacy outcomes, with wide intervals.
appraisal.one_line: A meta-analysis of five randomised trials testing noninferiority of left atrial appendage closure against medical therapy in atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: LAAC met noninferiority compared with medical therapy in atrial fibrillation for major bleeding (RR 0.86; 95% CI 0.59-1.26) and all-cause mortality (RR 0.93; 95% CI 0.71-1.22).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It overlaps with other recent LAAC pooled analyses and informs the choice between closure and anticoagulation.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Medical Therapy in Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver resection creates a clinical tension between limiting operative bleeding and maintaining organ perfusion. Low central venous pressure, fluid restriction, vascular inflow occlusion and vasoactive treatment can coincide with lower arterial pressure, yet existing reviews have centred on blood loss and transfusion. They have not resolved whether directly quantified intraoperative hypotension is associated with postoperative acute kidney injury or myocardial injury, or whether comparative haemodynamic strategies alter these outcomes. We will address both questions while keeping exposure associations distinct from management effects and kidney outcomes distinct from myocardial outcomes.
METHODS: This prospectively registered review will search four bibliographic databases and two trial registries from inception, supplemented by citation searching and author contact, without language or date restrictions. Eligible studies will include adults undergoing partial liver resection and report a quantified intraoperative arterial-hypotension exposure or a comparative pressure- or flow-directed strategy with acute kidney injury or myocardial injury. Two reviewers will independently select studies, extract data and assess risk of bias, with independent handling of review-team-authored studies. Four prespecified synthesis domains will separate exposure from management evidence and kidney from myocardial outcomes. Compatible estimates will undergo random-effects meta-analysis; otherwise, structured synthesis without meta-analysis will be used. Heterogeneity, missing evidence and certainty will be assessed. This design aims to distinguish prognostic association from evidence about modifiable haemodynamic management.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261476933; Open Science Framework https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/3GCY2.
title: Intraoperative hypotension and postoperative acute kidney injury or myocardial injury after liver resection: A protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a guideline-recommended treatment for severe aortic stenosis (AS). While the balloon-expandable Edwards Sapien 3 valve has long been the benchmark, the newer Myval valve has emerged as a potential alternative. Comparative data on mid-term survival, specifically one-year all-cause mortality, are lacking but crucial for clinical evaluation.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised direct comparative evidence on the Myval versus Sapien 3 valves in patients undergoing TAVI, searching PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central up to November 2025. The primary outcomes included all-cause mortality within 30 days and 1 year. Secondary outcomes were 30-day safety events and hemodynamic parameters.
RESULTS: Five studies (n = 2771) were included. The pooled analysis indicated no statistical difference in 30-day mortality (RR: 1.05, 95% CI: 0.53-2.07; p = 0.89; I2=0%) or in one-year all-cause mortality (RR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.64-1.35; p = 0.70; I2=0%). Rates of stroke, major bleeding, pacemaker implantation, and other 30-day complications were also comparable (all p > 0.05). Hemodynamically, the Myval valve was superior at 30 days, with a lower mean gradient (MD: -2.37, 95% CI: -3.45 to -1.30; p < 0.0001) and larger effective orifice area (MD: 0.26, 95% CI: 0.17-0.35; p < 0.00001). Available one-year data from two randomised trials indicated this hemodynamic benefit was sustained.
CONCLUSION: This updated meta-analysis demonstrates that the newer Myval valve offers comparable early safety and one-year survival to the established Sapien 3 valve, with superior and sustained hemodynamic performance. These findings support its role as a safe and effective alternative in the TAVI landscape.
title: Updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing Myval versus Sapien 3 transcatheter heart valves in severe aortic stenosis: focus on early and one-year mortality.

abstract: Use of Impella 5.5 in patients with decompensated heart failure-associated cardiogenic shock (ADHF-CS) is increasing as a bridge to advanced therapies. The effects of maximal trans-valvular unloading on biventricular filling and pressure-volume area (PVA) in ADHF-CS are poorly understood. Nine patients with medically refractory ADHF-CS underwent Impella 5.5 placement with simultaneous invasive arterial, venous, and biventricular pressure-volume loop analysis. Acutely after Impella 5.5 activation, cardiac output (3.4 ± 0.5 vs. 5.0 ± 0.7 L/min, p = 0.0011), diastolic (67.2 ± 8.0 vs. 80.7 ± 9.7 mm Hg, p = 0.0044) and mean arterial pressures (77.9 ± 7.1 vs. 86.9 ± 10.4 mm Hg, p = 0.029) increased, compared to baseline. Left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (24.1 ± 6.7 vs. 16.8 ± 5.4 mm Hg, p = 0.0027), volume (262.1 ± 103.9 vs. 231.5 ± 104.3 ml, p = 0.0036), and PVA (21,913 ± 7,055 vs. 18,357 ± 7,758 mmHg·ml, p = 0.013) decreased. Right ventricular end-diastolic (12.4 ± 4.6 vs. 9.1 ± 3.8 mm Hg, p = 3.8E-5) and end-systolic pressure (42.1 ± 11.9 vs. 34.4 ± 11.1 mm Hg, p = 0.030) and PVA (6,303 ± 3,851 vs. 4,437 ± 2,473 mm Hg·ml, p = 0.027) also decreased. These findings suggest that maximal left ventricular unloading can acutely reduce biventricular filling pressures and PVA in patients with ADHF-CS.
journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
title: Acute Effects of Impella 5.5 on Biventricular Filling and Pressure-Volume Area in Patients With Heart Failure Associated Cardiogenic Shock.

abstract:
AIM: Patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤35% are at high risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). The left atrial minimum volume index (LAVImin) and late gadolinium enhancement of the left ventricular myocardium (LGE) have each been reported as stand-alone predictors, but their combined risk stratification and incremental prognostic value in this specific population remains unclear.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective two-centre study included 338 patients with AMI and LVEF ≤35% (training cohort, n = 235; external validation cohort, n = 103) imaged by cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) between January 2014 and October 2024. Two blinded radiologists quantified LAVImin, LGE, and other CMR parameters. Cox regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis evaluated the separate and combined prognostic value of LAVImin and LGE. Five nested prediction models were developed and validated internally and externally.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 37 months, 55 of 235 training cohort patients (23.4%) experienced MACE. Patients with LAVImin ≥20.4 mL/m2 and LGE ≥29.5% had the poorest MACE-free survival (log-rank P < .001). The model combining clinical factors, conventional CMR risk factors, LAVImin and LGE (Model 5) discriminated best (apparent Harrell C statistic 0.77, optimism-corrected 0.73; external validation 0.78, calibration slope 0.96) and improved modestly but significantly on the conventional CMR model (Model 2; likelihood ratio P < .001, ΔAUC = 0.051, P = .04).
CONCLUSION: In patients with AMI and LVEF ≤35% who underwent CMR, combined LAVImin and LGE enable survival risk stratification and provide modest but significant incremental prognostic value for MACE.
title: Incremental prognostic value of left atrial minimum volume index and late gadolinium enhancement in acute myocardial infarction patients with left ventricular ejection fraction ≤35.
